India — States & Symbols — The 1971 war (3-16 December) was triggered by the Bangladesh Liberation movement in East Pakistan. India's intervention ended in Pakistan's surrender at Dhaka on 16 December 1971 — Lt Gen A.A.K. Niazi signed the Instrument of Surrender before Lt Gen Jagjit Singh Aurora; around 93,000 Pakistani soldiers became prisoners of war. 16 December is observed as Vijay Diwas. Myanmar (then Burma), Sri Lanka (Ceylon) and Bhutan already existed as separate states in 1971.

cards.front:
INDIA currently has how many STATES + UNION TERRITORIES?

(A) 25 + 5
(B) 28 STATES + 8 UTs
(C) 29 + 7
(D) 30 + 10
cards.back:
(B) 28 STATES + 8 UTs

India — States & Symbols — INDIA currently has 28 STATES + 8 UNION TERRITORIES (UTs) (2024). STATES (28 alphabetically — CAPITAL): (1) ANDHRA PRADESH — Amaravati (under construction) / currently de-facto Vijayawada-Visakhapatnam; Telugu. (2) ARUNACHAL PRADESH — ITANAGAR. (3) ASSAM — DISPUR (Guwahati); Assamese. (4) BIHAR — PATNA; Hindi. (5) CHHATTISGARH — RAIPUR (created 2000); Hindi. (6) GOA — PANAJI; Konkani. Smallest state. (7) GUJARAT — GANDHINAGAR. (8) HARYANA — CHANDIGARH (shared with Punjab — UT). (9) HIMACHAL PRADESH — SHIMLA; Hindi. (10) JHARKHAND — RANCHI (created 2000). (11) KARNATAKA — BENGALURU; Kannada. (12) KERALA — THIRUVANANTHAPURAM; Malayalam. (13) MADHYA PRADESH — BHOPAL. Largest state by area after Raj. (14) MAHARASHTRA — MUMBAI; Marathi. 2nd most populous. (15) MANIPUR — IMPHAL; Manipuri. (16) MEGHALAYA — SHILLONG; Khasi/English. (17) MIZORAM — AIZAWL; Mizo. (18) NAGALAND — KOHIMA; English. (19) ODISHA — BHUBANESWAR; Odia. (20) PUNJAB — CHANDIGARH (shared); Punjabi. (21) RAJASTHAN — JAIPUR. LARGEST state by area. (22) SIKKIM — GANGTOK; Nepali. Smallest population + 22nd state (1975 merger). (23) TAMIL NADU — CHENNAI; Tamil. (24) TELANGANA — HYDERABAD (shared with AP till 2014, full from 2024); Telugu. 29TH state created 2 JUN 2014. (25) TRIPURA — AGARTALA; Bengali. (26) UTTAR PRADESH — LUCKNOW; Hindi. MOST POPULOUS (~23 crore). If a country, would be 5th largest. (27) UTTARAKHAND — DEHRADUN (summer)/Gairsain (winter); Hindi. Formed 2000. (28) WEST BENGAL — KOLKATA; Bengali. UNION TERRITORIES (8): WITH LEGISLATURE: (a) DELHI (National Capital Territory; CM Arvind Kejriwal AAP 2013-, now 3rd term; 70 seats). (b) PUDUCHERRY (former French colonies, Puducherry + Mahé + Karaikal + Yanam; CM N Rangasamy AINRC 2021-; 30 seats). (c) J&K (since 31 Oct 2019; first elections Sep-Oct 2024; CM Omar Abdullah NC+Cong 2024-). WITHOUT LEGISLATURE (directly under President via LG/Administrator): (d) CHANDIGARH — shared capital Punjab+Haryana. (e) ANDAMAN + NICOBAR ISLANDS — Port Blair (renamed Shri Vijaya Puram in 2024). (f) LAKSHADWEEP — Kavaratti. (g) DADRA + NAGAR HAVELI + DAMAN + DIU (merged 26 Jan 2020; HQ Daman). (h) LADAKH (since 31 Oct 2019; Leh + Kargil; demands full statehood + 6th Schedule tribal protection). TOTAL = 36 (28+8). RECENT reorganisation: (a) 2014 (2 Jun) — TELANGANA formed from AP (29th state). (b) 2019 (31 Oct) — J&K state BIFURCATED into 2 UTs (J&K with LA + Ladakh without LA); Art 370 abrogated. (c) 2020 (26 Jan) — Dadra + NH + Daman + Diu UTs merged (had been separate). State count 28 + UT count 8. STATE ORDER OF CREATION: Andhra State (1953, first linguistic); Gujarat + Maharashtra (1960, from Bombay); Nagaland 1963; Haryana 1966; HP full state 1971; Meghalaya, Manipur, Tripura 1972; Sikkim 1975; Mizoram + Arunachal + Goa 1987; Chhattisgarh + Uttarakhand + Jharkhand 2000; Telangana 2014. PENDING state demands: Gorkhaland (WB), Vidarbha (Maharashtra), Bundelkhand, Bodoland, Harit Pradesh (UP), Kodagu, Greater Tipraland, Saurashtra, Mithilanchal, Kongu Nadu, Panruti. cards.front:
The LARGEST Indian state by AREA is:

(A) Uttar Pradesh
(B) RAJASTHAN
(C) Madhya Pradesh
(D) Maharashtra
cards.back:
(B) RAJASTHAN

India — States & Symbols — INDIAN STATES by AREA (top 10, 2024): (1) RAJASTHAN — 342,239 sq km (10.4%). Capital JAIPUR. Known for: Thar Desert (Sahara of India), Mughal-Rajput architecture, princely palaces, Pushkar camel fair, Kaziranga... er Ranthambore tigers. Bordered by Pakistan + 5 states. (2) MADHYA PRADESH — 308,252 sq km. Capital BHOPAL. 'Heart of India' — central India. Tiger reserves (Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Pench, Panna). Ujjain, Khajuraho (UNESCO), Gwalior, Indore (cleanest city 6 years). Highest tribal population state. (3) MAHARASHTRA — 307,713 sq km. Capital MUMBAI (financial capital of India; 'maximum city'); RTE + Bollywood + Ajanta-Ellora UNESCO + Shivaji's Raigad + Ganapati Pune + Nasik Kumbh. 2nd most populous state. (4) UTTAR PRADESH — 240,928 sq km. Capital LUCKNOW. MOST POPULOUS state (~23 crore). Taj Mahal + Varanasi + Ayodhya + Prayagraj Kumbh + Mathura + Agra. Has ~28% of nation's population on ~7% land. Divides into 75 districts; Hindi heartland. (5) GUJARAT — 196,024 sq km. Capital GANDHINAGAR. 'India's Jewel' business state. Modi home state. Statue of Unity (182m, world's tallest). Rann of Kutch + Gir lions. Surat diamond city. (6) KARNATAKA — 191,791 sq km. Capital BENGALURU (IT capital of India). Hampi, Coorg, Mysore. Kannada heritage + Bhakti saints. (7) ANDHRA PRADESH — 162,968 sq km (post-Telangana). Capital Amaravati (planned). Telugu heritage; Tirupati temple; Araku Valley. (8) ODISHA — 155,707 sq km. Capital BHUBANESWAR. Puri Jagannath, Konark, Chilika lake, Sun Temple, tribal culture + Kalinga legacy. (9) CHHATTISGARH — 135,192 sq km. Capital RAIPUR. Carved from MP 2000. Tribal heartland; Bastar, Jagdalpur. (10) TAMIL NADU — 130,058 sq km. Capital CHENNAI. Dravidian culture + Carnatic music + classical Tamil. STATES by POPULATION (top 10, 2011 census projected to 2024): (1) UP ~23 cr; (2) Maharashtra ~13 cr; (3) Bihar ~13 cr; (4) West Bengal ~10 cr; (5) MP ~8.6 cr; (6) TN ~8 cr; (7) Rajasthan ~8 cr; (8) Karnataka ~6.9 cr; (9) Gujarat ~6.8 cr; (10) Andhra ~5.2 cr. SMALLEST states: (a) by AREA — GOA (3,702 sq km; smallest state), SIKKIM (7,096 sq km); (b) by POPULATION — SIKKIM (~7 lakh; smallest), Mizoram, Arunachal. UTs by area: (a) Largest UT = LADAKH (59,146 sq km — larger than Kerala + Punjab); (b) Smallest UT = LAKSHADWEEP (32 sq km). MOST DENSELY POPULATED: Delhi UT (11,297/sq km), Bihar (1,106), WB (1,028), Kerala (859). LEAST DENSELY POPULATED: Arunachal (17/sq km), Mizoram (52), Sikkim (86), Manipur (128). INDIA's TOTAL AREA: 3,287,263 sq km = 7th largest country. INDIA's POPULATION: ~144 crore (2024, world's most populous since April 2023). 3,42,239 sq km (~10.4% of India's area); desert-heavy (Thar); capital Jaipur; largest by area since formation 1956.

cards.front:
The capital of ANDHRA PRADESH (post-Telangana split 2014) is:

(A) Visakhapatnam
(B) AMARAVATI
(C) Hyderabad (still)
(D) Tirupati
cards.back:
(B) AMARAVATI

India — States & Symbols — ANDHRA PRADESH CAPITAL SAGA — complex post-Telangana bifurcation (2 JUNE 2014). BACKGROUND: (1) Under ANDHRA PRADESH REORGANISATION ACT 2014, HYDERABAD was to be JOINT CAPITAL of AP + Telangana for 10 YEARS (till 2 JUN 2024; this deadline passed; now Hyderabad is solely Telangana's). (2) Residual AP had to build NEW CAPITAL. CM N. Chandrababu Naidu (TDP, 2014-19) chose AMARAVATI — greenfield city on south bank of Krishna river; adjacent to historic Amaravati (Buddhist heritage; capital of Satavahanas 2,000 yrs ago). Architects: Norman Foster + others (visionary design). Hindi World Capital funds + Singapore consultancy. Inaugurated capital city construction 2014-19. ~33,000 acres land pooled from farmers. Progress was made but... (3) 2019 — Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy (YSRCP) became CM; HALTED Amaravati + proposed '3 CAPITALS' — (a) AMARAVATI = LEGISLATIVE capital; (b) VISAKHAPATNAM = EXECUTIVE capital; (c) KURNOOL = JUDICIAL capital. Modelled on South Africa. Passed AP Decentralisation Acts 2020. Massive protests from Amaravati farmers (who had pooled land). HC struck down Acts 2022. Govt appealed to SC. STALEMATE throughout 2019-24. (4) 2024 (May-June) — TDP-Jana Sena-BJP alliance WON AP elections; N Chandrababu Naidu RETURNED as CM. Revived AMARAVATI as sole capital; Jan 2025 formally restored Amaravati Capital City masterplan. PROGRESS: Secretariat + Assembly + HC buildings under-construction (paused 2019-24); farmer trust to be restored. Target 2027-29 for usable capital. TEMP AP ARRANGEMENT: as of 2024-25, government operates partly from Vijayawada + Guntur (core Amaravati area); HC at Amaravati; some at Visakhapatnam. TRULY unique — probably world's MOST INTERRUPTED capital project. OTHER STATE CAPITAL MOVES in INDIAN HISTORY: (1) DELHI — shifted from Calcutta in 1911 (Delhi Durbar); inaugurated 1931. (2) CHHATTISGARH — new capital RAIPUR from formation 2000. (3) JHARKHAND — Ranchi from 2000. (4) UTTARAKHAND — DEHRADUN temporary since 2000; planned GAIRSAIN (Chamoli, Himalayan foothills) as summer capital since 2020. (5) HIMACHAL PRADESH — SHIMLA (from early 1864 British hill station — still India's busiest tourist hill station; now overcrowded). (6) RECENT demands: KARNATAKA ('Greater Bengaluru'), UP (Noida as hub)... NEW CAPITAL examples globally: (a) BRASILIA (Brazil, 1960) — Lucio Costa + Niemeyer. (b) CANBERRA (Australia, 1927). (c) ISLAMABAD (Pakistan, 1967). (d) DODOMA (Tanzania, 1974). (e) ABUJA (Nigeria, 1991). (f) ASTANA/NUR-SULTAN (Kazakhstan, 1997; restored to Astana 2022). (g) NAYPYIDAW (Myanmar, 2005, secretive). (h) NUSANTARA (Indonesia, 2024 — East Kalimantan, moving from Jakarta due to sinking + congestion). AMARAVATI is one of world's most ambitious + politically fraught greenfield capitals. India's earlier Naya Raipur, Gandhinagar, Chandigarh, Bhubaneswar are greenfield capitals. but political flux; Chandrababu Naidu revived Jan 2025 after YSRCP's 3-capital plan scrapped; planned greenfield capital on Krishna riverbank.

cards.front:
KERALA's capital is:

(A) Kochi
(B) THIRUVANANTHAPURAM
(C) Kozhikode
(D) Alappuzha
cards.back:
(B) THIRUVANANTHAPURAM

India — States & Symbols — KERALA ('God's Own Country' — tourism tagline) — one of India's most culturally + environmentally distinctive states. Capital: THIRUVANANTHAPURAM (formerly TRIVANDRUM). Name means 'abode of Ananta' (the serpent on which Vishnu reclines — from SRI PADMANABHASWAMY TEMPLE's deity). Southernmost state capital. KERALA FACTS: (1) FORMATION: 1 November 1956 (Kerala Piravi Day) — linguistic reorganisation combining Malabar (Madras) + Travancore + Cochin. (2) MALAYALAM — official language; palindrome name. (3) 38,863 sq km area; 3.5 crore population. (4) HIGHEST LITERACY RATE in India — 94% (NFHS-5); declared FULLY LITERATE 1991 by NLM; 2024 survey found effective 96%+. (5) Sex ratio 1,084 females/1000 males — BEST in India. (6) Highest LIFE EXPECTANCY — 75 years (national 70). (7) Lowest IMR (Infant Mortality Rate) — 4 per 1000 live births (national 27). (8) HDI rank 1 among Indian states. (9) KERALA MODEL of DEVELOPMENT — high human-development indicators despite middle per-capita income; achieved via land reforms + education + health investments + leftist + matrilineal Nair/Nampudri social traditions + remittances from Gulf. (10) REMITTANCES — ~20% of GSDP; 23+ lakh Keralite expatriates abroad (mostly Gulf). (11) ECONOMY — tourism + remittances + services dominant; agri (coconuts, spices, tea, rubber) + fisheries. (12) BACKWATERS — famous CANOE-DOTTED network of lagoons + lakes + rivers; Alappuzha/Alleppey + Kumarakom + Kottayam + Kollam; HOUSE BOATS popular tourist draw. (13) WESTERN GHATS — UNESCO WHS (2012). (14) 4 UNESCO WHS sites in Kerala's broader region. (15) HIGH OUTMIGRATION — best-educated youth leaving for jobs. (16) RESPECTFUL COMMUNISM — only Indian state where CPI(M) has sustained electoral base; LDF-UDF alternate rule; current LDF govt (Pinarayi Vijayan CM since 2016, 2021-26). MAJOR TOURIST DESTINATIONS: (a) THIRUVANANTHAPURAM — Padmanabhaswamy Temple (richest temple in world — vaults opened 2011 revealed $22 billion treasure). Napier Museum, Shanghumukham Beach, Kovalam beach. (b) KOCHI — commercial capital, port city. Mattancherry Palace + Jewish synagogue (Paradesi, 1568). Fort Kochi. Chinese fishing nets. Kochi-Muziris Biennale. (c) ALAPPUZHA (Alleppey) — 'Venice of the East'; backwaters + Nehru Trophy Boat Race. (d) MUNNAR — tea plantations in hills. (e) WAYANAD — wildlife + edakkal caves. (f) THEKKADY (Periyar) — wildlife sanctuary. (g) KUMARAKOM — backwaters + birds. (h) KOVALAM — beaches. (i) VARKALA — cliff beach. (j) BEKAL — Arabian Sea fort. (k) PARAMBIKULAM + SILENT VALLEY — biosphere reserves. (l) SABARIMALA — Ayyappa temple (pilgrimage site; 2018 SC-allowed women's entry ruling sparked protests). (m) CHERAI Beach. CUISINE: KERALA + BANANA CHIPS + PARATHA (CF PAROTTA/MALABAR) + CHICKEN STEW + APPAM + KADALA + meen moilee (fish) + sadhya (22-dish feast on banana leaf) + coconut every dish. OKU (onam) + VISHU + Christmas major festivals. ONAM — 10-day festival end-Aug/Sep celebrating King Mahabali's annual return. KATHAKALI + MOHINIYATTAM + KUDIYATTAM + KALARIPAYATTU martial art. MALAYALAM CINEMA — Adoor Gopalakrishnan, Shaji Karun, Aravindan, recent MANI RATNAM, Lijo Jose Pellissery, parallel cinema tradition. MAJOR AIRPORTS: Trivandrum + Kochi + Calicut + Kannur. Major PORTS: Cochin (oldest + transhipment hub) + Vizhinjam (Adani's new deepwater port, 2024). India's first indigenously-built Rocket-Launch Pad = TERLS Thumba Thiruvananthapuram. southern-most state capital; 'abode of Ananta (Vishnu)' Hindu mythology; seat of Kerala Legislative Assembly; formerly TRIVANDRUM.

cards.front:
India's 7 SISTER STATES of the NORTH EAST + 1 'brother' state are:

(A) Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, WB, Sikkim, Assam, Manipur, Tripura
(B) '7 SISTERS'
(C) Only 4 states
(D) 10 separate states
cards.back:
(B) '7 SISTERS'

India — States & Symbols — NORTH-EAST INDIA / NORTH EASTERN STATES — 8 states: the '7 SISTERS' + SIKKIM ('one brother'). (1) ASSAM (1 Apr 1912 as Assam Province; full state 1947); Capital DISPUR (Guwahati suburb). Largest NE state. Language: Assamese. GDP largest in NE. MANY indigenous groups; Tea + oil + tourism. Kaziranga (one-horned rhino UNESCO), Majuli (world's largest river island). (2) ARUNACHAL PRADESH (UT 1972 → State 20 Feb 1987). Capital ITANAGAR. 'LAND OF DAWN-LIT MOUNTAINS'. Largest NE state by area. 26 major tribes + 100 sub-tribes — most tribal diversity. Tawang monastery (biggest in India, 2nd in world; Dalai Lama's 1959 escape refuge). India-China border (disputed — Arunachal is claimed by China as 'South Tibet'). Close to Brahmaputra source. (3) MANIPUR ('jewel of India') — UT 1972 → State 21 Jan 1972. Capital IMPHAL. Language: Meiteilon (Manipuri). Sangai deer unique. LOKTAK LAKE + KEIBUL LAMJAO (world's only FLOATING national park). Famous WOMEN-only market (Ima Keithel, Imphal). Polo + Ras Leela + Thang-Ta martial art. INA HQ was here (Netaji's Provisional Govt). 2023 Meitei-Kuki communal violence (ongoing crisis). (4) MEGHALAYA ('abode of clouds') — carved from Assam 21 Jan 1972. Capital SHILLONG (Scotland of East). Language: Khasi (but English also official). WETTEST places in world — CHERRAPUNJI + MAWSYNRAM. Living root bridges (Khasi tribal engineering). DAWKI-Umngot river. Matrilineal (Khasi, Jaintia, Garo tribes — inheritance via youngest daughter). (5) MIZORAM (lit 'land of Mizo people') — UT 1972 → State 20 Feb 1987. Capital AIZAWL. Language: Mizo. ~87% Christian (highest among states); ~91% literate. Bamboo architecture + dances. HORTICULTURE hub. (6) NAGALAND — 1 Dec 1963 (16th state). Capital KOHIMA. Language: English (official; Nagamese is lingua franca). 16+ tribes — each with distinct culture + language. HORNBILL FESTIVAL (1-10 Dec, Kisama Heritage Village near Kohima) — showcase of all tribes. Battle of Kohima (1944) = turning point in WWII Burma campaign. (7) TRIPURA — UT 1972 → State 21 Jan 1972. Capital AGARTALA. Language: Bengali + Kokborok (tribal). Manikya dynasty ruled for 600+ years. (8) SIKKIM — 22ND STATE of INDIA (merged 16 MAY 1975 via referendum; earlier protectorate). Capital GANGTOK. Languages: Nepali, Bhutia, Lepcha (+ more). Kanchenjunga (Khangchendzonga) — India's tallest peak + world's 3rd tallest (8,586m; UNESCO Mixed Heritage since 2016); sacred to Sikkimese. FIRST fully ORGANIC farming state (2016). Bhutia + Lepcha + Nepali ethnic groups. NORTH EAST GOVERNANCE: 6TH SCHEDULE areas in (a) Meghalaya (Khasi, Jaintia, Garo Autonomous Councils); (b) Mizoram (Chakma, Mara, Lai Autonomous District Councils); (c) Tripura (TTAADC). 5TH SCHEDULE areas also. INSURGENCIES historically (now largely resolved): ULFA (Assam), NSCN (Nagaland — Naga Peace Accord 2015), HNLC (Meghalaya), DHD (Dima Hasao Assam), BLT/NDFB (Bodo Assam — 2020 Bodo Peace Accord). AFSPA (Armed Forces Special Powers Act 1958) still in force in parts. Infrastructure push: 100+ airports opened; BOGIBEEL BRIDGE (Assam 2018, India's longest rail-road bridge 4.94 km); Act East Policy (since 2014). ARUNACHAL PRADESH, ASSAM, MANIPUR, MEGHALAYA, MIZORAM, NAGALAND, TRIPURA + SIKKIM as 'brother' (8th NE state).

cards.front:
KANCHENJUNGA, India's TALLEST PEAK (8,586 m — world's 3rd tallest), is located on the border of:

(A) India + Pakistan
(B) SIKKIM (India) + NEPAL
(C) UP + Nepal
(D) J&K + China
cards.back:
(B) SIKKIM (India) + NEPAL

India — States & Symbols — KANCHENJUNGA (Khangchendzonga, 'Five Treasures of Snow') — 8,586 METRES (28,169 ft) — WORLD's 3rd HIGHEST MOUNTAIN + HIGHEST PEAK IN INDIA. Straddles SIKKIM-NEPAL border. First climbed 25 May 1955 by a British expedition (Joe Brown + George Band stopped just below the summit out of respect for the local Sikkimese belief that the summit is sacred — tradition continues; climbers still leave last few metres unclimbed). Name from Tibetan — 5 treasures of snow (gold, silver, gems, grain, holy books). KHANGCHENDZONGA NP — UNESCO MIXED Heritage site (2016, first in India for Mixed — natural + cultural); covers Kanchenjunga + 18 glaciers + diverse biodiversity + tribal sacred sites. 8000+ METRE PEAKS of the world (14 total, all in Himalayas + Karakoram, 'EIGHT-THOUSANDERS'): (1) MT EVEREST (8,848 m; Nepal-China; highest). (2) K2 (8,611 m; Pakistan-China; GILGIT-Baltistan area claimed by India as part of PoK). (3) KANCHENJUNGA (8,586 m). (4) Lhotse (8,516 m Nepal). (5) Makalu (8,481 m Nepal-China). (6) Cho Oyu (8,188 m Nepal-China). (7) Dhaulagiri (8,167 m Nepal). (8) Manaslu (8,163 m Nepal). (9) Nanga Parbat (8,126 m Pakistan). (10) Annapurna I (8,091 m Nepal). (11) Gasherbrum I (8,080 m; PoK). (12) Broad Peak (8,051 m; PoK). (13) Gasherbrum II (8,035 m; PoK). (14) Shishapangma (8,027 m; Tibet/China only — sole all-in-one-country 8000er; opened to climbers late). MOUNTAINS of INDIA (highest peaks by state, undisputed only — so excluding K2 + Gilgit peaks): (1) KANCHENJUNGA 8586 (Sikkim, India's tallest). (2) NANDA DEVI 7816 m (Uttarakhand; India's 2nd tallest; 2nd highest in India proper). (3) KAMET 7756 m (Uttarakhand). (4) SALTORO KANGRI 7742 m (Ladakh). (5) Mana Peak 7272 m (UK). (6) Mamostong Kangri 7516 (Ladakh). MINOR PEAKS: Munsiyari (UK), Roopkund (UK, mysterious skeletons lake), Chandra Taal (HP). MOUNTAINEERS from INDIA: (1) TENZING NORGAY — Sherpa (of Darjeeling Indian origin ambiguity, later Indian citizen); co-summit of Everest 29 May 1953 with Sir Edmund Hillary (NZ). Tenzing was IMF President 1954; Padma Bhushan 1959. (2) BACHENDRI PAL — FIRST INDIAN WOMAN on EVEREST (23 May 1984); 1st Indian + 5th woman in world. Padma Shri 1984, Padma Bhushan 2019. (3) SANTOSH YADAV — 1st woman TWICE on Everest (1992 + 1993). (4) ARUNIMA SINHA — 1st AMPUTEE WOMAN on Everest (2013; lost leg in train push by robbers 2011). (5) 13-year-old POORNA MALAVATH (Telangana, 2014) — youngest girl to summit Everest. (6) MALAVATH POORNA + SUSHMA SINGH + SATYARUP SIDDHANTA + various Army + IAF expeditions. INDIAN MOUNTAINEERING FOUNDATION (IMF, 1958, Delhi) regulates climbing. NEHRU INSTITUTE OF MOUNTAINEERING (NIM, Uttarkashi), HMI (Himalayan Mountaineering Institute, Darjeeling 1954 — Tenzing was founding director), ABVIMAS (Manali), JIM (Pahalgam), NIMAS (Sikkim) — key training institutes. highest peak in India; UNESCO Mixed Heritage Site (Khangchendzonga NP); sacred to Sikkimese; K₂ (higher) is in POK disputed area.

cards.front:
The FIRST STATE in INDIA to be created on PURELY LINGUISTIC basis was:

(A) Maharashtra
(B) ANDHRA STATE
(C) Punjab
(D) Gujarat
cards.back:
(B) ANDHRA STATE

India — States & Symbols — ANDHRA STATE — formed on 1 OCTOBER 1953 as FIRST LINGUISTIC state of independent India (Telugu-speaking majority carved from Madras State). Later merged with Telangana region of HYDERABAD state on 1 Nov 1956 (linguistic reorganisation) to form modern ANDHRA PRADESH. Further bifurcated 2014 into Andhra Pradesh + Telangana. POTTI SRIRAMULU (1901-1952) — Telugu linguistic leader; Gandhian + social reformer. His 56-DAY FAST-UNTO-DEATH at Madras demanding separate Andhra State led to his death on 15 DEC 1952 in a state of political indifference from Nehru + Congress. MASS UPHEAVAL in Andhra region after his death; riots; 7 killed in police firing. JAWAHARLAL NEHRU conceded — announced new Andhra state formation in Dec 1952; effective 1 OCT 1953. Sriramulu = 'AMARAJEEVI' ('immortal being'). This event CATALYSED the CONVENING of STATES REORGANISATION COMMISSION (SRC) in 1953 — Fazl Ali + K.M. Panikkar + H.N. Kunzru. Submitted report Oct 1955. STATES REORGANISATION ACT 1956 (1 Nov 1956) — India reorganised into 14 STATES + 6 UTs on PRIMARILY LINGUISTIC basis. LANGUAGES in India's 8TH SCHEDULE: (1) originally 14 at Constitution adoption 1950 — Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Kashmiri, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu. (2) Sindhi added 1967 (21st CAA). (3) Konkani + Manipuri + Nepali added 1992 (71st CAA). (4) Bodo + Dogri + Maithili + Santhali added 2003 (92nd CAA). Current: 22 SCHEDULED LANGUAGES. PENDING: RAJASTHANI, BHOJPURI, MAGAHI, TULU, KHASI, MIZO, GARO, KODAVA, KHORTHA, KUMAONI, GARHWALI, BHOJPURI, ENGLISH etc. demanded. CLASSICAL LANGUAGES (6 + new additions Oct 2024) — ministry of culture recognition with criteria (1500-2000 years old + independent traditions + ancient literature + not subsidiary): (1) TAMIL (2004 — first); (2) SANSKRIT (2005); (3) TELUGU (2008); (4) KANNADA (2008); (5) MALAYALAM (2013); (6) ODIA (2014). Added Oct 2024 (Modi cabinet): (7) MARATHI; (8) PALI; (9) PRAKRIT; (10) ASSAMESE; (11) BENGALI. HINDI not in classical (younger). OFFICIAL LANGUAGES: (a) UNION — HINDI (Devanagari) + ENGLISH (as per Official Languages Act 1963 for associate purpose, continuation via amendments). (b) STATE — various under Art 345 + 347; each state can notify its own. (c) Scheduled languages have protections under Art 344 (Official Language Commission) + Art 348 (SC + HC use) + Art 351 (Hindi development). LINGUISTIC ORGANISATION has been SUCCESSFUL + stabilising for India. States' cultural + political identity strengthened. Bilingual Bombay (split 1960 Gujarat + Maharashtra); Trilingual Punjab (split 1966 Punjab + Haryana + HP additions); Khasi+Jaintia+Garo tribal Meghalaya, Manipuri etc. Further linguistic/ethnic demands continue: BODOLAND (Assam Bodo), GORKHALAND (WB Nepali), KAMTAPUR (WB Koch-Rajbongshi), MITHILANCHAL (Maithili Bihar), TULUNADU (Tulu Karnataka), KONGU NADU (TN), VIDARBHA (Marathi Maha), KODAVA (Karnataka). carved from Madras State after POTTI SRIRAMULU's 56-day fast-unto-death for Telugu state; catalyst for States Reorganisation 1956; 1 October 1953.

cards.front:
The NEWEST (29th) state of INDIA is:

(A) Jharkhand
(B) TELANGANA
(C) Uttarakhand
(D) Chhattisgarh
cards.back:
(B) TELANGANA

India — States & Symbols — TELANGANA — 29TH STATE of INDIA; formed 2 JUNE 2014. Bifurcation of ANDHRA PRADESH via ANDHRA PRADESH REORGANISATION ACT 2014. Capital: HYDERABAD (shared with residual AP till 2 June 2024 per 10-year transition clause; now SOLELY Telangana's). Area: 112,077 sq km (12th largest). Population ~3.5 crore. Language: TELUGU. LONG demand — ~60 YEARS of struggle + mobilisation. BACKGROUND: (1) Telangana region = former HYDERABAD state (Nizam's dominion, integrated 1948). (2) Merged with Andhra (ex-Madras) to form ANDHRA PRADESH on 1 NOV 1956 per Gentleman's Agreement with safeguards for Telangana. (3) Safeguards not fully implemented; perception of discrimination by coastal Andhra + Rayalaseema elites in jobs, water, education, resources. (4) 1969 first Telangana agitation (Marri Chenna Reddy); Separate Telangana Praja Samithi. (5) 2001 — K. CHANDRASHEKAR RAO (KCR) split from TDP to form TELANGANA RASHTRA SAMITHI (TRS) with single-point agenda. (6) KCR's 11-day fast 2009 (Nov-Dec 2009) forced Centre (Chidambaram) to announce Telangana would be carved out. Rollback due to coastal Andhra agitation; years of turmoil. (7) Oct 2011 — 'Million March' Hyderabad. (8) 2014 — UPA-II govt pushed Bifurcation Bill through Parliament despite chaos (pepper spray incidents in LS); passed 18 Feb 2014. Presidential assent 1 March 2014. (9) 2 JUN 2014 — Telangana became 29th state; KCR sworn in as 1st CM; TRS won 2014 + 2018 elections. (10) 2023 Dec elections: CONGRESS won; A. REVANTH REDDY became CM (7 Dec 2023). KCR OUT. TRS renamed BHARAT RASHTRA SAMITHI (BRS) 2022 to go national. KEY FACTS: (1) Telangana has 33 districts (up from 10 initial). (2) First state in INDIA to offer ₹3L crore DBT farm welfare (RYTHU BANDHU since 2018 — ₹10,000/acre/year to farmers). (3) PADDY + cotton + turmeric + chilli top crops. (4) Hyderabad = 'CYBERABAD' + 'GENOME VALLEY' — IT + Pharma + biotech hub; Microsoft largest campus outside Redmond. (5) KALESHWARAM PROJECT — world's largest multi-stage lift irrigation (Godavari); cost ₹1 lakh crore; controversy. (6) TS-Kisan Call Centre, Mission Bhagiratha (drinking water), 2BHK free houses schemes. (7) Literacy ~66%. (8) Kakatiya Rudreshwara Ramappa Temple (Warangal) = UNESCO WHS 2021. (9) Charminar + Golconda + Mecca Masjid + Falaknuma Palace at Hyderabad. (10) Hyderabadi biryani + haleem — cuisine icons. POST-2014 state formation — ALL PENDING state demands renewed: (1) GORKHALAND (Darjeeling hill areas, WB); (2) BODOLAND (Assam); (3) VIDARBHA (Maharashtra); (4) HARIT PRADESH / PURVANCHAL / Bundelkhand (UP breakup 4-way per Mayawati 2011); (5) Saurashtra (Gujarat); (6) Mithila (Bihar); (7) Kongu Nadu (TN); (8) Coorg (Karnataka); (9) Greater Tipraland (Tripura); (10) Kosala (Odisha). Politically challenging — each state creation sets precedent. Govt of India wary post-Telangana. NITI AAYOG vs PLANNING COMMISSION (scrapped Jan 2015) — reflects Centre's cooperative-federalism push. EARLIER STATES chronologically: (1) 1953 AP; (2) 1956 big reorganisation; (3) 1960 Maharashtra + Gujarat; (4) 1963 Nagaland; (5) 1966 Haryana; (6) 1971 HP; (7) 1972 Meghalaya/Manipur/Tripura; (8) 1975 Sikkim (22nd); (9) 1987 Mizoram/Arunachal/Goa (25-26-27); (10) 2000 Chhattisgarh (26th)/Uttarakhand/Jharkhand (28th wait — actually 26, 27, 28); (11) 2014 Telangana (29th). formed 2 June 2014 (bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh); Hyderabad as shared capital till June 2024, now solely Telangana's; first CM K. Chandrashekar Rao.

(6) KCR's 11-day fast 2009 (Nov-Dec 2009) forced Centre (Chidambaram) to announce Telangana would be carved out. Rollback due to coastal Andhra agitation; years of turmoil. (7) Oct 2011 — 'Million March' Hyderabad. (8) 2014 — UPA-II govt pushed Bifurcation Bill through Parliament despite chaos (pepper spray incidents in LS); passed 18 Feb 2014. Presidential assent 1 March 2014. (9) 2 JUN 2014 — Telangana became 29th state; KCR sworn in as 1st CM; TRS won 2014 + 2018 elections. (10) 2023 Dec elections: CONGRESS won; A. REVANTH REDDY became CM (7 Dec 2023). KCR OUT. TRS renamed BHARAT RASHTRA SAMITHI (BRS) 2022 to go national. KEY FACTS: (1) Telangana has 33 districts (up from 10 initial). (2) First state in INDIA to offer ₹3L crore DBT farm welfare (RYTHU BANDHU since 2018 — ₹10,000/acre/year to farmers). (3) PADDY + cotton + turmeric + chilli top crops. (4) Hyderabad = 'CYBERABAD' + 'GENOME VALLEY' — IT + Pharma + biotech hub; Microsoft largest campus outside Redmond. (5) KALESHWARAM PROJECT — world's largest multi-stage lift irrigation (Godavari); cost ₹1 lakh crore; controversy. (6) TS-Kisan Call Centre, Mission Bhagiratha (drinking water), 2BHK free houses schemes. (7) Literacy ~66%. (8) Kakatiya Rudreshwara Ramappa Temple (Warangal) = UNESCO WHS 2021. (9) Charminar + Golconda + Mecca Masjid + Falaknuma Palace at Hyderabad. (10) Hyderabadi biryani + haleem — cuisine icons. POST-2014 state formation — ALL PENDING state demands renewed: (1) GORKHALAND (Darjeeling hill areas, WB); (2) BODOLAND (Assam); (3) VIDARBHA (Maharashtra); (4) HARIT PRADESH / PURVANCHAL / Bundelkhand (UP breakup 4-way per Mayawati 2011); (5) Saurashtra (Gujarat); (6) Mithila (Bihar); (7) Kongu Nadu (TN); (8) Coorg (Karnataka); (9) Greater Tipraland (Tripura); (10) Kosala (Odisha). Chandrashekar Rao.

cards.front:
INDIA's LONGEST river that is ENTIRELY WITHIN Indian borders is:

(A) Ganga
(B) GODAVARI
(C) Brahmaputra
(D) Yamuna
cards.back:
(B) GODAVARI

India — States & Symbols — GODAVARI — 'DAKSHINA GANGA' (SOUTH GANGA); INDIA's 2ND LONGEST river (after Ganga) + LONGEST entirely within Indian territory. LENGTH: 1,465 km. SOURCE: TRYAMBAKESHWAR (Nashik district, Maharashtra) — one of the 12 JYOTIRLINGAS of Shiva; elevation ~1,067m in Western Ghats. FLOWS: Maharashtra → Telangana → Andhra Pradesh; empties into BAY of BENGAL near ANTARVEDI / RAZOLE (East Godavari / Konaseema district, Andhra) forming large DELTA. MAJOR TRIBUTARIES: Pranhita (largest; joins near Kaleshwaram), Indravati (Chhattisgarh-Odisha-Maharashtra), Sabari (Odisha-AP), Wardha, Wainganga (which join to form Pranhita), Manjra, Penganga. DRAINAGE BASIN: ~3.13 lakh sq km (~10% of India). Largest Peninsular river basin. MAJOR DAMS + PROJECTS: Jayakwadi (Paithan, Maharashtra), Gangapur, Polavaram (Andhra, massive project; under construction decades). Sriram Sagar, Kaleshwaram (world's largest multi-stage lift irrigation, Telangana 2019). FAMOUS CITIES on banks: Nashik, Aurangabad, Bhadrachalam (Ram temple), Rajahmundry (twin bridge), Nanded (Sikh Takht Sachkhand). KUMBH MELA / SIMHASTHA — Nashik (1 of 4 Indian Kumbh cities, along Haridwar + Ujjain + Allahabad). INDIA's RIVERS SYSTEM: (1) HIMALAYAN RIVERS — perennial (fed by glaciers + monsoon; long courses): INDUS SYSTEM — Indus, Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej (5 rivers of Punjab 'pancha-ab' = 5 waters) — most of these flow into Pakistan (Indus Waters Treaty 1960 divides — India gets Eastern 3 Ravi + Beas + Sutlej; Pakistan gets Western 3 Indus + Jhelum + Chenab). GANGA SYSTEM — Ganga (Ganges, 2,525 km, source Gangotri; longest in India INCLUDING Bangladesh), YAMUNA (1,376 km; longest tributary of Ganga; source Yamunotri), Gomati, Ghaghra (Karnali Nepal source), Gandak, Kosi ('sorrow of Bihar' — shifts course; source Tibet), Ramganga, Chambal (Yamuna tributary). BRAHMAPUTRA SYSTEM — Brahmaputra (2,900 km total; 916 km in India as Dihang/Siang/Brahmaputra via Arunachal → Assam → Bangladesh where called Jamuna → joins Ganga as Padma → Bay of Bengal). SOURCE: MANASAROVAR lake Tibet (as YARLUNG TSANGPO). (2) PENINSULAR RIVERS — seasonal, monsoon-fed, shorter, faster. EAST-FLOWING (to Bay of Bengal — form deltas): GODAVARI (1,465 km), KRISHNA (1,400 km, source MAHABALESHWAR MH), KAVERI (800 km, source TALAKAVERI KA), MAHANADI (858 km, Odisha), BRAHMANI, SUBARNAREKHA, PENNA, PENNAR. WEST-FLOWING (to Arabian Sea — form estuaries, no deltas; flow through rifts): NARMADA (1,312 km, source AMARKANTAK MP), TAPI / TAPTI (724 km, source MULTAI MP; Narmada + Tapi flow through RIFT VALLEYS between Vindhya + Satpura). SABARMATI, MAHI, LUNI (only river of Rajasthan; drains into Rann). WEST COAST rivers of Kerala + Karnataka: Periyar, Bharatapuzha, Pamba, Sharavathi (Jog Falls). RIVERS by INDIAN LENGTH: (1) Ganga 2525 km total; ~1300 km in India proper (rest Bangladesh). (2) Godavari 1465 km — longest WHOLLY INDIAN. (3) Yamuna 1376 km. (4) Krishna 1400 km. (5) Narmada 1312 km. (6) Indus 3180 km total, ~710 km in India. (7) Brahmaputra 2900 total, 916 km in India. NATIONAL RIVER: GANGA (declared 2008 by UPA). NAMAMI GANGE (2014, Modi govt) — ₹30,000+ crore cleanup. Ganges is among MOST POLLUTED rivers — sewage, industrial waste, agri runoff, rituals. CLEANING progress mixed. YAMUNA — Delhi stretch dead zone; Yamuna Action Plan. RIVER-LINKING projects proposed (NWDA) — controversial. 1,465 km, 2nd longest in India (after Ganga), entirely within India; 'Dakshina Ganga' (South Ganga); source TRYAMBAKESHWAR Nashik.

cards.back:

India — States & Symbols — Before the August 2019 reorganisation (which converted J&K into UTs), the erstwhile J&K state had dual capitals: Srinagar (summer) + Jammu (winter) — the Durbar Move tradition since 1872. Maharashtra has Mumbai as capital and Nagpur as 'winter capital' (legislature session), but it is de jure one capital. cards.front:
The National Emblem of India is an adaptation of which ancient sculpture?

(A) The Nataraja of the Chola period
(B) The Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath
(C) The Nandi bull from Thanjavur
(D) The Kailasa temple sculpture at Ellora
cards.back:
(B) The Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath

India — States & Symbols — The National Emblem of India is based on the LION CAPITAL OF ASHOKA at Sarnath (UP) — a sculpture atop an Ashokan pillar (~250 BCE) commemorating Buddha's first sermon. The original capital shows FOUR ADDORSED LIONS standing on an abacus (carrying four animals — lion, elephant, galloping horse, bull — separated by chakras), all on an inverted lotus. In the emblem, only 3 lions are visible (4th is hidden behind). Motto: 'SATYAMEVA JAYATE' (Truth alone triumphs) from the Mundaka Upanishad (not visible in the original sculpture — added to the emblem). Adopted on 26 January 1950. The original Sarnath sculpture is housed in the Sarnath Museum. A much larger recreation was installed atop the new Parliament building in July 2022.

cards.front:
The Indian National Anthem 'Jana Gana Mana' was composed by Rabindranath Tagore. In which year was it officially adopted by the Constituent Assembly?

(A) 15 August 1947
(B) 24 January 1950
(C) 26 January 1950
(D) 13 December 1911
cards.back:
(B) 24 January 1950

India — States & Symbols — 'Jana Gana Mana' — written by Rabindranath Tagore originally in Bengali (titled 'Bharoto Bhagyo Bidhata', 1911); first sung at INC's Calcutta session on 27 December 1911 — was officially adopted as the NATIONAL ANTHEM by the Constituent Assembly on 24 JANUARY 1950 (two days before the Constitution came into force). Full anthem: 5 stanzas; only the FIRST stanza is the national anthem. Duration: 52 seconds (full) or 20 seconds (short version). Composition tune: 'Raga Alhaiya Bilawal'. Same author also wrote Bangladesh's national anthem 'Amar Shonar Bangla' (1906). India's NATIONAL SONG 'Vande Mataram' (from Bankim Chandra's novel Anandamath 1882) — also adopted 24 Jan 1950 with EQUAL status to the anthem — famously sung at 1896 Calcutta INC session by Tagore himself.

cards.front:
Who designed the Indian National Flag (its final 3-colour horizontal tricolour form adopted in 1947)?

(A) Mahatma Gandhi
(B) Pingali Venkayya
(C) Madam Bhikaji Cama
(D) Nandalal Bose
cards.back:
(B) Pingali Venkayya

India — States & Symbols — PINGALI VENKAYYA (1876-1963, Andhra Pradesh) — an Indian freedom fighter, agriculturist, and Gandhian — designed the basic pattern of the Indian national flag. The final tricolour (saffron-white-green with the Ashoka Chakra in navy blue at centre) was ADOPTED on 22 JULY 1947 by the Constituent Assembly. Earlier flag versions: MADAM BHIKAJI CAMA unfurled an early tricolour on 22 Aug 1907 at Stuttgart (Germany, Intl Socialist Congress) — 1st 'Indian' flag on foreign soil. Gandhi's 1921 design had red (later saffron), white, green with a charkha. Nandalal Bose — illustrator of the Constitution's manuscript. Colour meanings: Saffron = courage/sacrifice; White = peace/truth; Green = faith/fertility; Chakra = Dharma/motion. Ratio 2:3. BIS standard for hand-spun khadi only.

(A) Blue whale
(B) Gangetic river dolphin
(C) Olive Ridley turtle
(D) Saltwater crocodile
cards.back:

India — States & Symbols — GANGETIC RIVER DOLPHIN (Platanista gangetica, locally 'Susu' / 'Soons' in Bihar) was declared India's National Aquatic Animal on 5 October 2009 by PM Dr. Manmohan Singh. Found in Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna-Karnaphuli river systems. Endangered (IUCN). Blind — navigates via echolocation. Population ~3500. Project Dolphin launched 2020 (like Project Tiger). cards.front:
Who designed the Indian rupee symbol '₹', and in which year was it officially adopted by the Government of India?

(A) Nandalal Bose; 1950
(B) D. Udaya Kumar; 2010
(C) Pingali Venkayya; 1947
(D) Satyajit Ray; 1982
cards.back:
(B) D. Udaya Kumar; 2010

India — States & Symbols — D. UDAYA KUMAR (IIT Guwahati faculty member, native of Kallakurichi TN) designed the rupee symbol '₹' — selected from ~3000 entries in a 2009 competition. Officially adopted on 15 JULY 2010 by the Union Cabinet. The symbol combines Devanagari 'र' (Ra) and Roman capital 'R' without the vertical line — featuring two parallel horizontal strokes on top (signifying India's tricolour or the '=' of equality). Before 2010, India used 'Rs.' Unicode code point U+20B9. India joined other major currencies with symbols: $ USD, € Euro, £ GBP, ¥ Yen, ₩ Won, ₹ Rupee (Sri Lanka and Nepal use their own). Thousand-separator: Indian system uses lakhs/crores (1,00,000 = 1 lakh, 10,00,00,000 = 10 crore); the Western system uses thousands/millions.

cards.front:
India's National Calendar is based on which calendar, effective since 22 March 1957?

(A) Vikrami Samvat
(B) Saka Samvat (Saka Era)
(C) Hijri (Islamic) Calendar
(D) Gregorian Calendar
cards.back:
(B) Saka Samvat (Saka Era)

India — States & Symbols — India's NATIONAL CALENDAR is the SAKA CALENDAR (Saka Samvat), adopted on 22 March 1957 based on the Calendar Reform Committee report (1952, chaired by Meghnad Saha). Year 1 of Saka era = 78 CE (commemorating Kanishka's coronation per one theory). First month = CHAITRA (starts 22 March, 21 March in leap year). Second month = VAISHAKHA, etc. Used officially for Gazette, AIR broadcasts, official calendars, some government communications. Current year: Saka 1946/47 (depending on month in 2024-25). Other Indian calendars: VIKRAM SAMVAT (year 1 = 57 BCE, still popular in Hindu tradition, 57 years ahead of CE), KALIYUGA era (3102 BCE start), Bengali calendar (Bongabdo), Tamil calendar, Malayalam (Kollam era), Saka-Kaliyug. International standards: Gregorian (civil/official), ISO 8601.

cards.front:
When was the Ganga declared India's National River, and during which anniversary was the declaration?

(A) 2004 — 50th anniversary of Republic Day
(B) 2008 — declared by the Union Cabinet
(C) 2014 — 125th birth anniversary of Gandhi
(D) 2019 — 70th anniversary of Constitution adoption
cards.back:
(B) 2008 — declared by the Union Cabinet

India — States & Symbols — The GANGA was declared India's NATIONAL RIVER on 4 November 2008 by the Union Cabinet, led by PM Manmohan Singh — and on the same day, the National Ganga River Basin Authority (NGRBA) was constituted under the Environment Protection Act 1986 to clean the river. Later, the NATIONAL MISSION FOR CLEAN GANGA (NMCG, 2011) and the broader NAMAMI GANGE programme (2014, ₹20,000 Cr initial allocation) have been key initiatives. The Ganga flows ~2525 km through 5 states: Uttarakhand (Bhagirathi from Gangotri Glacier + Alaknanda → union at Devprayag → 'Ganga' thereafter), UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, WB. Enters Bangladesh as Padma → Jamuna (Brahmaputra) → Meghna → Bay of Bengal. Ganga + Yamuna basin covers 25% of India's land and supports 40%+ of the population.

cards.front:

(B) Nile (Egypt/Sudan/Uganda)
(C) Yangtze (China)
(D) Mississippi (USA)
cards.back:
(B) Nile (Egypt/Sudan/Uganda)

India — States & Symbols — NILE — 6,650 km (4,130 miles), traditionally considered the world's longest river. Flows NORTH through 11 African countries (Uganda, South Sudan, Sudan, Egypt, Ethiopia, etc.) → Mediterranean. Two main tributaries: WHITE NILE (primary — from Lake Victoria) + BLUE NILE (from Ethiopian highlands, Lake Tana — carries 85% of water). AMAZON (~6,400 km) — long contested as the longest; 2014 Brazilian study claimed 6,992 km (making it longer), but measurement methodology disputed. Amazon has the LARGEST discharge by far (20% of world's fresh water into oceans). cards.back:

Contains the MARIANA TRENCH with CHALLENGER DEEP — deepest point on Earth at ~10,935 m (35,876 ft) — deeper than Mt Everest is tall! Challenger Deep, ~10,935 m.

cards.back:

LARGEST SALTWATER LAKE: Caspian. LAKES WITHIN LAKES (nested): Manitoulin Island's Lake Manitou within Lake Huron. cards.front:
The FASTEST LAND animal is:

(A) Lion
(B) Cheetah
(C) Greyhound
(D) Pronghorn antelope
cards.back:
(B) Cheetah

India — States & Symbols — CHEETAH (Acinonyx jubatus) — fastest land animal, hits 110-112 km/h (70 mph) in short bursts (3-4 sec). Reaches 100 km/h from standstill in ~3 seconds (faster than most supercars). Adaptations: long legs, spine-like muscles, non-retractable claws (grip), long tail (balance), large nostrils + heart/lungs. Second-fastest: PRONGHORN ANTELOPE (USA, ~88 km/h but for LONGER duration, several km). SPRINGBOK (~88 km/h). Other speeds: Lion 80 km/h; Greyhound 72 km/h; Horse 55-70 km/h. FASTEST in AIR: PEREGRINE FALCON (~389 km/h in hunting stoop dive — fastest animal overall). FASTEST in WATER: BLACK MARLIN (~129 km/h) or SAILFISH. SLOWEST: three-toed sloth (~0.24 km/h). Cheetahs nearly extinct by 1970s India; CHEETAHS REINTRODUCED from Namibia + SA to Kuno NP (MP) in 2022-23 via Project Cheetah. up to 112 km/h.

cards.front:
The Apatani tribe, famous for their nose-plug tradition and sustainable rice-fish farming, inhabits which state?

(A) Meghalaya
(B) Arunachal Pradesh
(C) Nagaland
(D) Manipur
cards.back:
(B) Arunachal Pradesh

India — States & Symbols — The Apatani (or Tanw) live in the Ziro Valley of Lower Subansiri district, Arunachal Pradesh. Famous for: (1) the facial 'Yapping Hulo' tradition (now discontinued — older Apatani women had large nose plugs and facial tattoos, done historically to make them 'unattractive' to raiding tribes); (2) sustainable wet-rice and fish (paddy-cum-pisciculture) farming on valley floors without using any animal power or wheel — a UNESCO candidate site for cultural landscape; (3) the Dree festival (July). The Apatani language belongs to the Tani branch of Sino-Tibetan.

cards.front:
The Khasi, Jaintia, and Garo are the three major indigenous tribes of which state?

(A) Nagaland
(B) Meghalaya
(C) Mizoram
(D) Tripura
cards.back:
(B) Meghalaya

India — States & Symbols — Meghalaya ('abode of clouds') has three major tribes inhabiting three hill regions: KHASI (central Khasi Hills — language is Khasian, an Austroasiatic language unique in NE), JAINTIA (eastern Jaintia Hills), and GARO (western Garo Hills — Tibeto-Burman language). All three are MATRILINEAL societies (inheritance through the mother's line — one of the largest surviving matrilineal societies in the world). The Khasis and Jaintias consider themselves 'Hynñiewtrep' (seven huts); the Garos call themselves 'A·chik'.

cards.front:
The term PVTG (Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group) was introduced in India during which period, and how many PVTGs are officially recognised?

(A) 1975 (as 'Primitive Tribal Groups'); 52 PVTGs
(B) 1975 (as PTGs, renamed PVTGs in 2006); 75 PVTGs
(C) 1991; 100 PVTGs
(D) 2011 Census; 45 PVTGs
cards.back:
(B) 1975 (as PTGs, renamed PVTGs in 2006); 75 PVTGs

India — States & Symbols — PVTGs were first recognised in 1975 (under the Dhebar Commission recommendation) as 'Primitive Tribal Groups' (PTGs); renamed PARTICULARLY VULNERABLE TRIBAL GROUPS in 2006. Currently 75 PVTGs are officially listed across 18 states + A&N Islands. Criteria for PVTG status: (a) pre-agricultural technology; (b) stagnant/declining population; (c) low literacy; (d) economic backwardness. Odisha has the MOST PVTGs (13), followed by Andhra Pradesh. Among PVTGs: Great Andamanese, Jarawa, Onge, Sentinelese (all A&N); Birhor, Saura, Korwa; Chenchu (AP); Toda (TN); Bhil-Koli; Sahariya.

The Toda tribe, known for their distinctive barrel-vaulted huts and buffalo-centric culture, inhabits which hill region?

(A) Aravalli Hills, Rajasthan
(B) Nilgiri Hills, Tamil Nadu
(C) Sahyadri Hills, Maharashtra
(D) Shevaroy Hills, Tamil Nadu
cards.back:
(B) Nilgiri Hills, Tamil Nadu

India — States & Symbols — The Toda (or Todar) are a small pastoral community of the Nilgiri Hills (Tamil Nadu), famous for: (1) half-barrel 'munds' (thatched huts without doors or windows; entry through a small opening); (2) sacred buffalo-based culture and associated dairy rituals; (3) intricate embroidered 'Pugur' shawls (GI-tagged). Population is tiny (~1500). Recognised as a PVTG. The Badaga, Kota, Irula, and Kurumba also inhabit the Nilgiris — studied extensively by anthropologists.

Construction: 1948-63; inaugurated by JAWAHARLAL NEHRU who called India's dams 'TEMPLES OF MODERN INDIA'. Creates GOBIND SAGAR reservoir (named after 10th Sikh Guru Gobind Singh) — 168 km² surface, 90km long. BHAKRA-NANGAL is the PAIR: Nangal Dam is 13km downstream (a barrage for irrigation + flood regulation). Power: 1325 MW total generation. Irrigates 10 million acres in Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan. Managed by BBMB (Bhakra Beas Management Board). Bhakra Main Canal feeds Indira Gandhi Canal system in Rajasthan. Called 'NEW TEMPLE OF INDIA' by Nehru (1963 speech). DAM vs BARRAGE distinction: Dam is tall, stores water; barrage is low-height with gates, diverts/regulates. in Bilaspur district, HP-Punjab border.

cards.front:
Nehru called dams the 'TEMPLES OF MODERN INDIA'. The FIRST major post-Independence multi-purpose river-valley project was:

(A) Bhakra Nangal (completed 1963)
(B) DAMODAR VALLEY CORPORATION (DVC)
(C) Rihand Dam
(D) Sardar Sarovar
cards.back:
(B) DAMODAR VALLEY CORPORATION (DVC)

India — Infrastructure — DVC (Damodar Valley Corporation) — established 7 July 1948, India's FIRST multi-purpose river valley authority. Modeled after the USA's TENNESSEE VALLEY AUTHORITY (TVA, 1933, New Deal). Objective: harness the DAMODAR RIVER (formerly 'Sorrow of Bengal' — caused frequent floods) for flood control, irrigation, hydroelectric power, coal-based thermal power, soil conservation. DAMS built under DVC: TILAIYA (Barakar river, 1953), KONAR (Konar river, 1955), MAITHON (Barakar, 1957), PANCHET (Damodar, 1959). Together with barrages at Durgapur + Bermo. Damodar used to cause huge annual floods in Bengal; DVC largely tamed it. Covers parts of Jharkhand + West Bengal. Significance: MAJOR pioneer in India's planned development + river valley development. Today, DVC also runs thermal + power trading. BHAKRA NANGAL came later (1963) — Nehru's famous 'Temples of Modern India' quote about Bhakra. RIHAND on Son river (Sonebhadra, UP) — built 1954-62. INDIRASAGAR, SARDAR SAROVAR etc. are all later. modeled on Tennessee Valley Authority, established 1948.

cards.front:
The INDIRA GANDHI CANAL (IGC) — the LONGEST canal in India — flows through which state, bringing water from the Sutlej-Beas river system to arid areas?

(A) Punjab
(B) RAJASTHAN
(C) Haryana
(D) Gujarat
cards.back:
(B) RAJASTHAN

India — Infrastructure — INDIRA GANDHI CANAL (IGC) — formerly RAJASTHAN CANAL; renamed 1984 in honour of Indira Gandhi. LONGEST canal in India: ~650 km (plus ~1,750 km of branches). Originates from HARIKE BARRAGE (at Sutlej-Beas confluence, Punjab — 40 km long Rajasthan Feeder Canal goes through Ferozepur + into Ganganagar district Rajasthan). Flows through: Ganganagar, Hanumangarh, Churu, Bikaner, Jaisalmer, Jodhpur, Barmer (NW Rajasthan — the Thar desert edge). Transformed arid desert lands into agricultural regions — wheat, cotton, mustard, gram now grown. CONCEIVED by Kanwar Sain (1948, engineer). Construction STARTED 1958 (1st phase inaugurated 1961 by Nehru). Phase 2 (to Jaisalmer) completed 1986. Criticism: waterlogging + salinity in some areas; ecological + sociological disruption; not reached easternmost target areas. Still India's greatest irrigation project by length/coverage. OTHER MAJOR CANALS: UPPER GANGA CANAL (world's largest irrigation canal system when built 1854 by Proby Cautley); SUTLEJ-YAMUNA LINK (SYL) — partially built, litigated Punjab-Haryana; NARMADA MAIN CANAL from Sardar Sarovar (458 km). transforms Thar desert fringe — Ganga Nagar, Hanumangarh, Bikaner, Jaisalmer.

cards.front:
The NARMADA BACHAO ANDOLAN (NBA) — a grassroots social movement opposing big dams — particularly targeted the Sardar Sarovar Project. Who was its primary leader?

(A) Vandana Shiva
(B) MEDHA PATKAR
(C) Sunderlal Bahuguna
(D) Chandi Prasad Bhatt
cards.back:
(B) MEDHA PATKAR

India — Infrastructure — NARMADA BACHAO ANDOLAN (NBA, 'Save the Narmada Movement') — a social movement launched 1989, primarily led by MEDHA PATKAR (Magsaysay Award 1992, Right Livelihood Award 1991). BABA AMTE (revered social activist, leprosy work) also supported. NOVELIST ARUNDHATI ROY wrote influential essays supporting it. Objections: (1) displacement of ~300,000 tribal + local people; (2) inadequate rehabilitation; (3) submergence of forests + fertile lands; (4) benefits more to rich farmers in far-off Gujarat than to affected peoples in MP/Maharashtra. SC case Narmada Bachao Andolan v. Union (2000): SC allowed continued construction with conditions on rehabilitation. Height was raised in phases. SARDAR SAROVAR finally inaugurated at full height in 2017 by PM Modi. OTHER ECO-MOVEMENTS: CHIPKO MOVEMENT (1970s, Uttarakhand, led by Sunderlal Bahuguna + Chandi Prasad Bhatt + Gaura Devi — hugged trees to save forests); SILENT VALLEY MOVEMENT (1970s-80s, Kerala, KSSP against hydroelectric project in Silent Valley rainforest — SUCCESS, dam cancelled, area became national park); APPIKO (1983, Karnataka, inspired by Chipko); JUNGLE BACHAO (Jharkhand); TEHRI DAM PROTESTS. along with Baba Amte, Arundhati Roy support.

cards.front:
The MULLAPERIYAR DAM — a century-old dam — has been a source of dispute between which two Indian states?

(A) Maharashtra and Karnataka
(B) Kerala (where the dam is located) and Tamil Nadu
(C) Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
(D) Punjab and Haryana
cards.back:
(B) Kerala (where the dam is located) and Tamil Nadu

India — Infrastructure — MULLAPERIYAR DAM — on PERIYAR RIVER in IDUKKI DISTRICT, KERALA. Built 1895 by the British (John Pennycuick, engineer) — 120+ years old. LEASED to Madras Presidency for 999 years under a 1886 treaty between Travancore + British. Since Independence, TAMIL NADU (successor to Madras) continues to OPERATE the dam and DIVERT Periyar waters through a tunnel under the Western Ghats to the Vaigai basin (for irrigation in Theni, Madurai). KERALA owns the land + surrounding area; wants the old dam decommissioned + replaced due to safety concerns (earthquake-prone zone, old lime-surki masonry). TAMIL NADU wants the dam preserved + water level raised (for its farmers). SC multiple rulings generally favouring TN's operational rights. Other inter-state water disputes: CAUVERY (Karnataka-TN-Puducherry-Kerala), KRISHNA (Maharashtra-Karnataka-AP-Telangana), GODAVARI (inter-state tribunal); RAVI-BEAS-SUTLEJ (Punjab-Haryana-Rajasthan — Sutlej Yamuna Link canal dispute). Under Art 262 + Inter-State River Water Disputes Act 1956, tribunals resolve such disputes — though often appealed in SC. which leases + operates it.

(6) BRITISH POUND (GBP) ≈ 1.25 USD. (7) CAYMAN ISLANDS DOLLAR ≈ 1.20 USD. (8) SWISS FRANC (CHF) ≈ 1.10 USD. EURO and US Dollar typically around 1.05-1.10. NOTE: ‘HIGHEST-VALUED’ does NOT mean ‘STRONGEST’ / ‘BEST PERFORMING’ — value vs USD is just a peg choice; Japan's YEN has nominally low per-unit value (~150 JPY = 1 USD) but JPY is a major reserve currency and economically strong. LOWEST-VALUED currencies (per USD): IRANIAN RIAL, VIETNAMESE DONG, SIERRA LEONE LEONE, LAOTIAN KIP, INDONESIAN RUPIAH, UZBEKISTANI SOM — all around or above 10,000 units per USD (inflation-eroded). INDIA’S RUPEE: ~₹85 = 1 USD (2026). Currency strength != economic strength; tiny Gulf states with fixed pegs look 'strong' but are tiny economies. 1 KWD ≈ 3.25 USD; highest-valued currency in the world due to oil wealth + pegged to a basket.

cards.front:
The capital of SWITZERLAND is:

(A) Zurich (largest city, financial centre)
(B) Geneva (diplomatic hub — UN, WHO, WTO, Red Cross HQ)
(C) BERN — de facto ‘federal city’ (no official ‘capital’ in constitution, but hosts parliament & government)
(D) Lucerne
cards.back:
(C) BERN — de facto ‘federal city’ (no official ‘capital’ in constitution, but hosts parliament & government)

International & Organizations — BERN (Swiss German ‘Bärn’) — DE FACTO CAPITAL of Switzerland; officially called the ‘FEDERAL CITY’ (Bundesstadt). Swiss constitution does NOT designate a formal ‘capital’ — reflects Swiss federalist ethos where cantons are equal. Bern hosts the FEDERAL ASSEMBLY (parliament), FEDERAL COUNCIL (executive), and the FEDERAL SUPREME COURT (in Lausanne, actually). Bern old town is UNESCO World Heritage (1983) — medieval arcades, clock tower Zytglogge. CURRENCY: SWISS FRANC (CHF, ‘Confoederatio Helvetica Franc’); symbol ‘Fr.’ or ‘sFr.’. Switzerland never joined the EURO; retains Franc as safe-haven currency; known for banking secrecy (reformed since FATCA 2014). OTHER MAJOR SWISS CITIES: (1) ZURICH — largest city, financial/banking capital; HQ of UBS, Credit Suisse (merged into UBS 2023). (2) GENEVA — DIPLOMATIC HUB — hosts UN European HQ ‘Palais des Nations’, WHO, WTO, ILO, UNHCR, IOM, ITU, WMO, WIPO, IPU, IOM, ICRC (Red Cross, founded 1863 by Henry Dunant — Nobel Peace 1901), CERN (on Franco-Swiss border). (3) LAUSANNE — IOC HQ, Federal Supreme Court, Olympic Museum. (4) BASEL — pharma hub (Novartis, Roche), Bank for International Settlements (BIS). SWISS OFFICIAL LANGUAGES: 4 — German (63%), French (23%), Italian (8%), Romansh (<1%). Swiss neutrality since 1815 (Congress of Vienna). Joined UN only in 2002.

cards.front:
Which currency is shared by over 20 European countries and is the SECOND-most traded in the world after the US Dollar?

(A) British Pound Sterling
(B) EURO (€, ISO EUR) — introduced 1999 as electronic currency; notes/coins 2002; 20 Eurozone countries as of 2026 (Croatia joined 2023)
(C) Swiss Franc
(D) Swedish Krona
cards.back:
(B) EURO (€, ISO EUR) — introduced 1999 as electronic currency; notes/coins 2002; 20 Eurozone countries as of 2026 (Croatia joined 2023)

International & Organizations — EURO (€, ISO CODE EUR) — single CURRENCY of the EUROZONE (Economic and Monetary Union of the EU). Introduced: (a) 1 JAN 1999 — as electronic/accounting currency; (b) 1 JAN 2002 — physical euro banknotes + coins circulated, replacing national currencies (franc, mark, lira, peseta, etc.). 20 COUNTRIES as of 2026 — 19+ CROATIA (joined 1 Jan 2023): AUSTRIA, BELGIUM, CYPRUS, CROATIA, ESTONIA, FINLAND, FRANCE, GERMANY, GREECE, IRELAND, ITALY, LATVIA, LITHUANIA, LUXEMBOURG, MALTA, NETHERLANDS, PORTUGAL, SLOVAKIA, SLOVENIA, SPAIN. (BULGARIA announced entry 1 Jan 2026.) EU members NOT in Eurozone: Bulgaria (joined 2026), Czechia, Denmark, Hungary, Poland, Romania, Sweden. UK: was in EU 1973-2020 (Brexit) but NEVER in Eurozone. MANAGED BY: EUROPEAN CENTRAL BANK (ECB), HQ Frankfurt am Main, Germany. First ECB President: Wim Duisenberg; currently: CHRISTINE LAGARDE (since 2019, first female; formerly IMF MD). EURO is 2nd-most traded currency (after USD), 2nd-largest reserve currency (~20% of global reserves vs USD's ~59%). Currency before euro: German MARK, French FRANC, Italian LIRA, Spanish PESETA, Dutch GUILDER, Portuguese ESCUDO, Greek DRACHMA, Irish PUNT, Finnish MARKKA, Austrian SCHILLING, Belgian/Luxembourg FRANC. EURO TOP: MONACO, SAN MARINO, ANDORRA, VATICAN CITY use the euro by agreement even though not EU members. Montenegro and Kosovo use it unilaterally.

cards.front:
The currency ‘NGULTRUM’ is used in which country?

(A) Nepal (Rupee)
(B) BHUTAN — NGULTRUM (Nu., BTN); pegged at par (1:1) with Indian Rupee (INR), and INR is also legal tender in Bhutan
(C) Myanmar (Kyat)
(D) Mongolia (Tugrik)
cards.back:
(B) BHUTAN — NGULTRUM (Nu., BTN); pegged at par (1:1) with Indian Rupee (INR), and INR is also legal tender in Bhutan

International & Organizations — NGULTRUM (Nu., ISO BTN) — currency of BHUTAN since 1974 (when Bhutan established its monetary system). Pegged at PAR (1:1) with INDIAN RUPEE (INR). INR is also LEGAL TENDER in Bhutan (₹500 and ₹2000 notes have been subject to limits). 1 Ngultrum = 100 Chhertum (like paise). Issued by: ROYAL MONETARY AUTHORITY OF BHUTAN (RMA, est. 1982), Thimphu. Bhutan's banknotes feature images of the dzongs (fortress monasteries) and the Dragon King (‘Druk Gyalpo’). BHUTAN at a glance: (1) Capital: THIMPHU (the only world capital without traffic lights — traffic cops only); (2) Largest city: Thimphu; (3) Monarchy: Kings of the Wangchuck dynasty since 1907; current king JIGME KHESAR NAMGYEL WANGCHUCK (5th Druk Gyalpo, crowned 2008); (4) Geography: landlocked Himalayan, between India & China; (5) Religion: Vajrayana Buddhism (state religion); (6) Famous for: GROSS NATIONAL HAPPINESS (GNH, constitutional goal since 1972, 9 domains, 4 pillars); (7) Major exports: hydroelectricity (mostly to India), cardamom, gypsum; (8) Connectivity: only 1 international airport at PARO (famously difficult approach). OTHER ‘INDIA-PEGGED’ or Indian Rupee-linked currencies: NEPALI RUPEE (1 INR = 1.6 NPR, fixed since 1993); MALDIVIAN RUFIYAA (not pegged). SIMILAR-SOUNDING but DIFFERENT: Mongolian TUGRIK, Uzbek SUM, Myanmar KYAT, Cambodian RIEL, Laotian KIP.

cards.front:
ANKARA is the capital of which country?

(A) Greece (capital: Athens)
(B) TURKEY — capital since 1923 when Mustafa Kemal Atatürk moved it from Istanbul/Constantinople to symbolise the new Republic
(C) Jordan (capital: Amman)
(D) Iran (capital: Tehran)
cards.back:
(B) TURKEY — capital since 1923 when Mustafa Kemal Atatürk moved it from Istanbul/Constantinople to symbolise the new Republic

International & Organizations — ANKARA — capital of TURKEY since 13 OCTOBER 1923 (proclaimed by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk at the founding of the Republic of Turkey). PREVIOUSLY: the OTTOMAN capital was CONSTANTINOPLE (renamed ISTANBUL in 1930) — which is still Turkey's largest city and economic hub. Atatürk moved capital to Ankara to symbolise the break from Ottoman past, move toward the Anatolian heartland, and because Istanbul was vulnerable to attack (near straits). Population ~5 million; Istanbul ~15 million. Ankara hosts the PRESIDENT, GRAND NATIONAL ASSEMBLY, SUPREME COURT; Atatürk's mausoleum ANITKABIR is here. Currency: TURKISH LIRA (TRY, ₺) — has suffered massive inflation (revalued 2005, currently undergoing high inflation again since 2021). TURKEY: trans-continental — 3% Europe (East Thrace), 97% Asia; straits of BOSPORUS, SEA OF MARMARA, and DARDANELLES separate the two; Istanbul is the only city in the WORLD on 2 CONTINENTS. NATO member since 1952; EU candidate since 1999 (stalled); applied again 2024. Geography: borders 8 countries — Greece, Bulgaria, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan (Nakhichevan), Iran, Iraq, Syria. Mt ARARAT — highest point (5,137 m). Cappadocia, Pamukkale, Ephesus (ancient Ionian city), Troy — tourist draws. Recent: Feb 2023 Turkey-Syria earthquake (>50,000 dead).

cards.front:
THIMPHU is famous for being one of the very few world capitals WITHOUT:

(A) An international airport
(B) A railway station
(C) TRAFFIC LIGHTS / signals
(D) A shopping mall
cards.back:
(C) TRAFFIC LIGHTS / signals

International & Organizations — THIMPHU — capital of BHUTAN, and widely cited as ‘the only world capital without TRAFFIC LIGHTS’. The capital tried installing signals in 1999 but residents disliked the impersonal feel and reverted to traditional POLICE HAND-SIGNALLING at intersections — now the tourist attraction itself. Thimphu population ~1.15 lakh; country population ~7.8 lakh. No traffic light until at least 2025. BHUTAN broadly: landlocked Himalayan monarchy; 5th King JIGME KHESAR NAMGYEL WANGCHUCK (since 2006). (A) Parliament: National Assembly + National Council (bicameral). (B) National sport: ARCHERY (‘dha’). (C) National animal: TAKIN. (D) National flower: BLUE POPPY (Meconopsis). (E) National bird: RAVEN. (F) National tree: CYPRESS. (G) ‘GROSS NATIONAL HAPPINESS’ (GNH) — concept coined by King Jigme Singye Wangchuck (4th) in 1972 — 4 pillars (sustainable development, environment, culture, good governance), 9 domains, GNH INDEX created 2008. (H) FOREIGN RELATIONS: special relationship with INDIA under 2007 Treaty of Friendship (updated from 1949); Indian Rupee is legal tender; India manages Bhutan's defence. (I) No diplomatic ties with UNITED NATIONS Permanent Members (UK, USA, Russia, China, France) — Bhutan has NO embassies in USA or China. (J) UN member since 1971. OTHER notable ‘quirky’ capitals: LA PAZ (Bolivia) — highest administrative capital (3,600 m); FUNAFUTI (Tuvalu) — smallest; VATICAN CITY — smallest state & capital; SAN MARINO city — in one of world's oldest republics. police officers manually direct traffic with hand signals.

cards.front:
Which country's currency is the DONG?

(A) Thailand
(B) Cambodia
(C) VIETNAM
(D) Indonesia
cards.back:
(C) VIETNAM

International & Organizations — VIETNAMESE DONG (Đồng, symbol ₫, ISO VND) — currency of VIETNAM since 1978 when North & South Vietnam currencies were unified (North had used dong since 1946; South had used piastre → southern dong). Issued by the STATE BANK OF VIETNAM, HQ HANOI. Currently around ~25,000 VND per 1 USD (2026) — one of the LOWEST per-unit value currencies globally (inflation-eroded). A ‘new dong’ has been mooted but not implemented. 1 VND = 10 hao = 100 xu (subdivisions rarely used). Modern notes feature HO CHI MINH (the revolutionary founding father). VIETNAM overview: (a) Capital: HANOI (northern, political); largest city: HO CHI MINH CITY (southern, formerly Saigon, economic hub); (b) Area: ~331,000 sq km (S-shaped along South China Sea / East Sea); (c) Population: ~100 million (world's 16th most-populous); (d) Government: single-party socialist republic under Communist Party of Vietnam; (e) Key rivers: RED RIVER (Hanoi delta), MEKONG (Saigon delta); (f) History: French Indochina colony until 1954; Vietnam War (1955-75) ended with communist North taking over the South; economic ‘DOI MOI’ reforms since 1986; joined ASEAN 1995, WTO 2007. NEIGHBOURING SE ASIA currencies: CAMBODIA — RIEL (KHR); LAOS — KIP (LAK); THAILAND — BAHT (THB); MYANMAR — KYAT (MMK); MALAYSIA — RINGGIT (MYR); INDONESIA — RUPIAH (IDR); PHILIPPINES — PESO (PHP); SINGAPORE — SGD; BRUNEI — Brunei Dollar (BND, pegged 1:1 with SGD). ‘Đồng’ (₫, VND); issued by State Bank of Vietnam; one of the world's weakest currencies per unit (~25,000 VND = 1 USD in 2026).

cards.front:
The capital of NEW ZEALAND is:

(A) Auckland (largest city)
(B) Christchurch
(C) WELLINGTON
(D) Queenstown
cards.back:
(C) WELLINGTON

International & Organizations — WELLINGTON — capital of NEW ZEALAND; located at the southern tip of the NORTH ISLAND on the shore of Cook Strait. SELECTED as capital in 1865 (moved from Auckland, the original capital post-1841) because of its CENTRAL LOCATION relative to the two islands, as South Island settlers complained Auckland was too remote. Population ~215,000 (city); metropolitan area ~420,000; 3rd-largest metro area in NZ after Auckland and Christchurch. Known as the ‘WINDY CITY’ due to Cook Strait winds; nicknamed ‘Welly’. Hosts Parliament of NZ (famous ‘BEEHIVE’ executive wing — architect Sir Basil Spence 1977), Government House (Governor-General's residence), Supreme Court, Cabinet, most Civil Service HQ. Also hosts TE PAPA Tongarewa (Museum of New Zealand), the National Film Archive, Victoria University. Sir PETER JACKSON's WETA WORKSHOP + Weta Digital (Lord of the Rings VFX) are based here. NEW ZEALAND factsheet: (a) Currency: NEW ZEALAND DOLLAR (NZ$, ISO NZD) — introduced 1967, decimal; also used in Cook Islands, Niue, Tokelau, Pitcairn. (b) Prime Minister: CHRISTOPHER LUXON (National Party, since 2023). (c) King: Charles III (Commonwealth realm). (d) Languages: English, Māori (reo Māori), NZ Sign Language (all official). (e) Area: 268,000 sq km (similar to UK). (f) Major cities: Auckland (largest, 1/3 of population), Wellington (capital), Christchurch (Canterbury, South Island), Hamilton, Tauranga. (g) Geography: two main islands (North + South) + many smaller; divided by Cook Strait; South Island dominated by SOUTHERN ALPS + Mt. COOK/Aoraki (3,724 m, highest). on the southern tip of the North Island; one of the southernmost national capitals in the world (41° S).

cards.front:
The United Nations was established in 1945. Where is its headquarters located?

(A) Geneva, Switzerland
(B) New York City, USA
(C) The Hague, Netherlands
(D) Paris, France
cards.back:
(B) New York City, USA

International & Organizations — The UN was established on 24 October 1945 (after 50 founding members ratified the Charter). HQ is in New York City (extraterritorial status — not under US jurisdiction). cards.front:
The World Trade Organization (WTO) was established in 1995, replacing which earlier agreement?

(A) International Trade Organization (ITO)
(B) General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)
(C) Bretton Woods Agreement
(D) Marshall Plan
cards.back:
(B) General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)

International & Organizations — The WTO was established on 1 January 1995 following the Marrakesh Agreement (1994) that concluded the Uruguay Round of GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, 1947) negotiations. WTO REPLACES GATT as a formal institution but retains GATT as one of its covered agreements (for goods). Other WTO covered agreements: GATS (services), TRIPS (intellectual property), DSU (dispute settlement understanding). HQ: Geneva. Current DG: Dr. Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (Nigeria — first woman and first African, appointed March 2021). 164 members. India has been challenging many WTO decisions on agricultural subsidies, digital trade, MSP. The 'Appellate Body' is currently dysfunctional due to US blocking new appointments since 2019.

cards.front:
The G20 (Group of Twenty) PRESIDENCY was held by INDIA in:

(A) 2024
(B) 1 Dec 2022
(C) 2025
(D) 2015
cards.back:
(B) 1 Dec 2022

International & Organizations — G20 (GROUP of TWENTY) — FORUM of 20 MAJOR ECONOMIES — 19 countries + European Union + (since 2023) African Union. Founded 1999 (FINANCE MINISTERS) after Asian Financial Crisis 1997. Elevated to LEADERS SUMMIT level in 2008 (post-Global Financial Crisis). MEMBERS (19 nations): Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, France, Germany, India, Indonesia, Italy, Japan, Mexico, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, South Korea, Turkey, UK, USA + EU. Represents ~85% of global GDP, 75% of trade, 2/3 of world population. Presidency ROTATES annually. INDIA's PRESIDENCY (1 DEC 2022 – 30 NOV 2023): THEME 'VASUDHAIVA KUTUMBAKAM' ('The World is One Family') from Maha Upanishad; subtitle 'ONE EARTH, ONE FAMILY, ONE FUTURE'. LOGO: LOTUS + Earth. KEY PRIORITIES: (1) Green Development + climate finance + LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment). (2) Accelerated, Inclusive + Resilient Growth. (3) SDG Acceleration. (4) Technological Transformation + Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) — India's UPI + Aadhaar model showcased. (5) Multilateral Institutions Reform — push for UN + UNSC reform. (6) Women-Led Development. G20 SUMMIT in NEW DELHI, 9-10 SEPTEMBER 2023 — at BHARAT MANDAPAM (Pragati Maidan). Heads of State + Governments attended (except Xi Jinping + Putin who skipped — sent premiers). KEY OUTCOMES: (1) NEW DELHI LEADERS' DECLARATION — UNANIMOUS consensus (rare feat given Russia-Ukraine + US-China tensions; called diplomatic 'COUP' for Indian Sherpa AMITABH KANT). (2) AFRICAN UNION admitted as PERMANENT MEMBER — 21st member; India pushed strongly. G20 now informally 'G21'. (3) INDIA-MIDDLE-EAST-EUROPE ECONOMIC CORRIDOR (IMEC) — announced; rail + shipping route India → UAE → Saudi → Israel → EU; counter to China's BRI. (4) Global Biofuels Alliance launched. (5) Digital Public Infrastructure framework + Aadhaar-UPI-ONDC promoted. (6) Finance Track — MDB reform, crypto regulation, debt restructuring. (7) Climate — tripling renewables by 2030. (8) ACCEPTANCE of India's Sherpa leadership; India chaired ~200 meetings in 60 cities. (9) Gandhi at Rajghat tribute by leaders. (10) CULTURAL showcase — kala + food + yoga. BRAZIL 2024 Presidency: theme 'Building a Just World + Sustainable Planet'. Rio summit Nov 2024. SOUTH AFRICA 2025 (current). USA 2026 (Trump's return affects vibe). G20 SUMMITS: (1) 2008 Washington (first, crisis response); (2) 2009 London + Pittsburgh; (3) 2010 Toronto + Seoul; ... cards.front:
The SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) was founded in:

(A) 1947
(B) 8 December 1985 at Dhaka
(C) 1971
(D) 2001
cards.back:
(B) 8 December 1985 at Dhaka

International & Organizations — SAARC (SOUTH ASIAN ASSOCIATION FOR REGIONAL COOPERATION) — regional intergovernmental organisation of 8 South Asian countries. FOUNDED: 8 DECEMBER 1985 at the 1st SAARC Summit in DHAKA, Bangladesh. 8 DECEMBER = SAARC Charter Day. Idea proposed by BANGLADESH's President ZIAUR RAHMAN in 1980. 7 FOUNDING members: BANGLADESH, BHUTAN, INDIA, MALDIVES, NEPAL, PAKISTAN, SRI LANKA. AFGHANISTAN joined APRIL 2007 as 8th member (at 14th SAARC Summit New Delhi). HQ: KATHMANDU (Nepal). COVERS: 3% of world's area + 21% of world's population (~2 billion people) + only 4% of world's GDP — demonstrates under-integration. OBJECTIVES (Charter): (1) Promote welfare + economic growth + social progress + cultural development in region. (2) Strengthen collective self-reliance. (3) Promote + strengthen mutual trust, understanding + appreciation of one another's problems. (4) Contribute to mutual trust + cooperative aims. STRUCTURE: (a) SUMMITS — annually supposed, but INFREQUENT due to India-Pakistan tensions. (b) COUNCIL OF MINISTERS. (c) STANDING COMMITTEES. (d) TECHNICAL Committees. (e) SECRETARIAT at Kathmandu headed by SECRETARY-GENERAL (3-year term, rotated). SAARC SUMMITS HELD: 1st Dhaka 1985 → 18th KATHMANDU 2014. Subsequent 19th summit planned for ISLAMABAD 2016 — CANCELLED after URI TERROR ATTACK (Sept 2016; India + 3 others boycotted citing Pakistani terror). SAARC in HIBERNATION since — NO SUMMIT for 10 years (as of 2024-25). INDIA + Pakistan rivalry major roadblock. KEY AGREEMENTS: (1) SAARC Preferential Trading Arrangement (SAPTA, 1993) + SAARC Free Trade Area (SAFTA, 2006, in force Jan 2006). Tariff reduction phased. (2) SAARC FOOD BANK 2007 for food security. (3) SAARC Development Fund (SDF) 2010 — Thimphu. (4) SAARC Framework Agreement for Energy Cooperation 2014. (5) SAARC Convention on Narcotic Drugs (1990) + Suppression of Terrorism (1987). ACHIEVEMENTS LIMITED: only ~5-7% intra-regional trade (vs ASEAN 25%, EU 60%); low connectivity; low FDI between member countries. CHALLENGES: (1) India-Pakistan conflict overshadowing everything. (2) Low priority from Pakistan for SAARC. (3) Smaller neighbours (Nepal, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh) sometimes feel Indian dominance concern. (4) Bhutan + Bangladesh + Nepal + Sri Lanka (BBIN) sub-regional cooperation rising as alternative. (5) China's BRI + CPEC expanding. BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical + Economic Cooperation) — formed 1997; 7 members: India + Bangladesh + Bhutan + Myanmar + Nepal + Sri Lanka + Thailand; Pakistan + Afghanistan + Maldives NOT in it. Seen as potential SAARC alternative bypassing Pakistan. BIMSTEC Summit 2022 Colombo. BBIN (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal) — 2015 onwards; motor vehicles agreement (Bhutan's parliament still not ratified). INDIA's 'NEIGHBOURHOOD FIRST' POLICY (2014) — prioritises South Asian ties but bypasses Pakistan. Modi's inauguration 2014 + 2019 attended by SAARC leaders (except Pakistan in 2019 due to tensions). INDIA'S regional aid: (a) Neighbourhood Development Partnership Grant. (b) Vaccine Maitri (COVID vaccines to SAARC + world). (c) Pipelines (India-Nepal MOTIHARI-AMLEKHGANJ 2019), rail links, development aid. (d) LOCs (lines of credit) to Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Maldives, Bhutan. 7 founding members (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka); Afghanistan joined 2007 (8 members); HQ Kathmandu.

cards.front:
BRICS was EXPANDED on 1 January 2024 with 5 NEW MEMBERS. The expanded 'BRICS+' now comprises:

(A) Only original 5 (Brazil/Russia/India/China/S Africa)
(B) 10 members
(C) G7 countries
(D) UK + France added
cards.back:
(B) 10 members

International & Organizations — BRICS — major grouping of emerging economies. FOUNDING 4 (BRIC): BRAZIL + RUSSIA + INDIA + CHINA. Term coined 2001 by Jim O'Neill of GOLDMAN SACHS in paper 'Building Better Global Economic BRICs'. Formal cooperation begun 2006 (UN-level meeting) + first full summit 2009 YEKATERINBURG Russia. SOUTH AFRICA joined 2010 — making BRICS (5 members). EXPANSION — BRICS+ announced at 15th SUMMIT JOHANNESBURG SOUTH AFRICA (22-24 Aug 2023): invited 6 new members — EGYPT, ETHIOPIA, IRAN, UNITED ARAB EMIRATES, SAUDI ARABIA, ARGENTINA. From 1 JANUARY 2024 they formally joined EXCEPT Argentina (new President Javier Milei, elected Dec 2023, rejected invitation — pro-Western pivot). Saudi Arabia status somewhat pending (slow movement). So BRICS+ = ORIGINAL 5 + 4-5 NEW = ~10 MEMBERS. REPRESENTS: ~45% of world population; ~35% of global GDP (PPP); ~25% nominal; major share of global reserves + oil + grain. OBJECTIVES: (1) Political dialogue + cooperation. (2) Economic + trade ties. (3) Alternative to Western-dominated IMF + World Bank + G7. (4) Multi-polar world order. (5) Financial autonomy from USD / SWIFT. KEY INSTITUTIONS (not equivalent to UN but emerging): (1) NEW DEVELOPMENT BANK (NDB) — est. 2014 SHANGHAI Summit; HQ SHANGHAI (CHINA). Offers loans for infrastructure + sustainability in BRICS + developing countries; alternative to World Bank. India's KV KAMATH was 1st President 2015-20. (2) CONTINGENT RESERVE ARRANGEMENT (CRA) — $100 BILLION currency swap fund for BRICS + EMs facing BoP crises; counter to IMF. Also BRICS PAY + BRICS Stock Exchange Forum + BRICS University League. SUMMITS: (1) 1st 2009 Yekaterinburg; (2) 2010 Brasília; (3) 2011 Sanya China; (4) 2012 New Delhi India; (5) 2013 Durban; (6) 2014 Fortaleza Brazil; (7) 2015 Ufa Russia; (8) 2016 GOA India; (9) 2017 Xiamen China; (10) 2018 Joburg; (11) 2019 Brasília; (12) 2020 virtual (COVID); (13) 2021 virtual India chair; (14) 2022 Beijing virtual; (15) 2023 JOBURG (expansion announced); (16) 2024 KAZAN RUSSIA (Putin's first major summit post-Ukraine invasion); (17) 2025 RIO BRAZIL; (18) 2026 India chair. KAZAN SUMMIT (22-24 Oct 2024) Oct highlights: (1) 'Kazan Declaration' + 'partner country' category introduced (expansion BRICS+). (2) India-China LAC disengagement just prior (Modi-Xi bilateral first since 2019 Doklam-Galwan). (3) India pushed for BRICS payment system — reducing USD dependence; de-dollarisation discussion. Currency talk (own currency, commodity-backed) rejected by India though not formally. (4) Russia highlighted strategic autonomy + criticism of Western sanctions. CURRENT BRICS+ RANKINGS: (a) China — world's 2nd economy by nominal GDP. (b) India — 5th. (c) Russia — 11th. (d) Brazil — 9th. (e) S Africa — 35th. Among new: Saudi Arabia 17th, UAE 33rd, Egypt 35th, Iran 38th, Ethiopia 50s. QUAD — parallel grouping with DIFFERENT member composition: USA + Japan + India + Australia. Strategic security focus against China's Indo-Pacific footprint. I2U2: India + Israel + UAE + USA (2022 'West Asia Quad'). Other EMERGING — G77 (developing countries, ~134); NAM (non-aligned); IBSA (India-Brazil-S Africa 2003); SCO (Shanghai Cooperation Organisation — China-led, 9 members including India + Pakistan). original 5 + EGYPT + ETHIOPIA + IRAN + UAE + Saudi Arabia (joining officially but status pending); Argentina declined under Milei.
