cards.front:
The QUAD (Quadrilateral Security Dialogue) includes:

(A) India + Russia + China + Pakistan
(B) USA + JAPAN + AUSTRALIA + INDIA
(C) EU countries only
(D) All NATO members
cards.back:
(B) USA + JAPAN + AUSTRALIA + INDIA

International & Organizations — QUAD / QUADRILATERAL SECURITY DIALOGUE — strategic partnership of 4 countries: USA + JAPAN + AUSTRALIA + INDIA. 'Indo-Pacific Quad'. Focus: democratic values, maritime security, counter-balancing China's rise. ORIGINS: (1) 2004 Indian Ocean TSUNAMI response — coordinated humanitarian response by these 4 countries (with later addition of Indonesia, Singapore, N Zealand). (2) FORMALISED 2007 — Japan's PM SHINZO ABE proposed 'Confluence of 2 Oceans' speech in Indian Parliament (Aug 2007 — spoke of Indo-Pacific connectedness); QUAD DIALOGUE begun 2007 with all 4 + naval MALABAR 2007 exercise (Bay of Bengal). (3) WITHERED 2007-17 — Australia withdrew under Rudd (Labor, pro-China); India under UPA-II cautious. (4) REVIVED 2017 Manila ASEAN sidelines — Trump + Abe + Modi + Turnbull resurrected dialogue. (5) 2020 onwards — intensified; elevated to LEADERS level. 6 QUAD LEADERS' SUMMITS: (1) March 2021 virtual (inaugural; Biden + Suga + Morrison + Modi). (2) Sep 2021 in-person Washington. (3) May 2022 Tokyo (Kishida). (4) Mar 2023 virtual. (5) May 2023 Hiroshima sideline (with G7). (6) Sep 2024 WILMINGTON, DELAWARE (Biden's home; hosted after Quad summit in India was delayed). Planned 2025 India summit. KEY INITIATIVES: (1) QUAD VACCINE PARTNERSHIP — initially pandemic response; India produces (Bharat Biotech Covaxin + SII Covishield); US + Japan funding; Australia logistics. Delivered 600M+ vaccine doses Indo-Pacific. (2) Quad INFRASTRUCTURE PARTNERSHIP — counter to China BRI. (3) Quad CLIMATE Working Group. (4) Quad TECH (critical + emerging tech; 5G, AI, semiconductors; export controls). (5) Quad CYBER + SPACE. (6) IPMDA (Indo-Pacific Maritime Domain Awareness) — monitor illegal fishing + vessels. (7) Quad QUAD FELLOWSHIP — 100 students/year in STEM. (8) MALABAR NAVAL EXERCISE — originally India-US (1992); expanded to India-US-Japan (2015); then Australia rejoined (2020 onwards, at India's invitation) — so QUAD navies now drill together regularly. WHY IT MATTERS: (a) RESPONSE to CHINA's expansion — South China Sea, Taiwan pressure, BRI, island-chain buildup. (b) FREEDOM of NAVIGATION + overflight in Indo-Pacific. (c) Democratic values alliance. (d) SUPPLY CHAIN diversification post-COVID. (e) Tech standards vs China-dominated tech norms. CHINA opposes QUAD vehemently — calls it 'Asian NATO' + 'Cold War mentality'. INDIA IS CAREFUL not to label Quad anti-China officially; prefers 'for' free Indo-Pacific rather than 'against' China; maintains STRATEGIC AUTONOMY + nonaligned tradition; participates in both QUAD + BRICS + SCO — unique multi-alignment. Critics say Quad is 'MILITARY-LIGHT' (not a formal alliance; no mutual defence clause); supporters say this flexibility is its STRENGTH. AUKUS (Australia + UK + US, 2021) — separate trilateral SECURITY PACT; AUSTRALIA to get NUCLEAR SUBMARINES via US + UK tech transfer. France furious over cancelled Australian contract. Some see AUKUS as Quad+. RELATED groupings: (1) I2U2 (India + Israel + UAE + USA, 2022) — 'West Asian Quad'. (2) 'CHIP 4' (USA, Japan, S Korea, Taiwan) — semiconductors. (3) G7 + IPEF (Indo-Pacific Economic Framework, 2022) — 14 economies including India. (4) ASEAN + Plus grouping (ASEAN + China, Japan, Korea = APT). NATO — USA-led 32-member military alliance (original 1949 + expansions; Finland 2023, Sweden 2024 latest; Ukraine's bid aggravated Russia invasion). NATO's 'INDO-PACIFIC PARTNERS' = Japan, S Korea, Australia, NZ — increasing engagement. RUSSIA-NATO standoff = backbone of Ukraine conflict. Indo-Pacific strategic alignment; revived 2017; Leaders' summits since 2021; focus on China's rise.

cards.front:
The NON-ALIGNED MOVEMENT (NAM) was founded in:

(A) 1945 with UN
(B) 1961 at BELGRADE
(C) 1955 Bandung
(D) 2010
cards.back:
(B) 1961 at BELGRADE

International & Organizations — NAM (NON-ALIGNED MOVEMENT) — forum of developing countries NOT FORMALLY ALIGNED with any major power bloc during COLD WAR. FOUNDED 1961 at 1ST SUMMIT in BELGRADE (Yugoslavia, 1-6 Sept 1961) with 25 founding members. KEY FOUNDERS — '5 Fathers of NAM': (1) JAWAHARLAL NEHRU — India; PM; chief architect; 5 Principles of Peaceful Coexistence (Panchsheel 1954) + Bandung Spirit. (2) JOSIP BROZ TITO — Yugoslavia; independent socialist; defied Stalin. (3) GAMAL ABDEL NASSER — Egypt; pan-Arabism; Suez nationalised 1956. (4) SUKARNO — Indonesia; hosted 1955 Bandung Asian-African Conference. (5) KWAME NKRUMAH — Ghana; pan-African; Africa's 1st president post-independence. PREDECESSOR event: BANDUNG CONFERENCE (18-24 April 1955, Indonesia) — 29 Asian + African newly-independent states met; 'Dasasila Bandung' (10 principles); seeded NAM movement. KEY PRINCIPLES of NAM (from Belgrade): (1) Mutual RESPECT for territorial integrity + sovereignty. (2) MUTUAL NON-AGGRESSION. (3) Non-interference in internal affairs. (4) EQUALITY + MUTUAL BENEFIT. (5) PEACEFUL COEXISTENCE. (6) NEUTRALITY between USSR + USA. MEMBERSHIP CRITERIA: (1) Policy of independence based on peaceful coexistence + non-alignment. (2) Consistently supporting national independence movements. (3) Not member of multilateral MILITARY ALLIANCE tied to great-power conflicts (US-led NATO or Soviet-led Warsaw). (4) Not member of bilateral military pact with great power. CURRENT: 120 MEMBERS (states) + 17 OBSERVERS + 10 observer organisations = LARGEST intergovernmental grouping after UN. Covers 55% of world's population. INDIA is founding member + ACTIVE. SUMMITS held every 3 YEARS. Chair rotates alphabetically. SUMMIT HISTORY: (1) 1961 Belgrade; (2) 1964 Cairo; (3) 1970 Lusaka Zambia; (4) 1973 Algiers; (5) 1976 Colombo; (6) 1979 HAVANA; (7) 1983 DELHI (Indira Gandhi chaired after coup against Bishop in Grenada); (8) 1986 Harare; (9) 1989 Belgrade; (10) 1992 Jakarta; (11) 1995 Cartagena; (12) 1998 Durban; (13) 2003 Kuala Lumpur; (14) 2006 Havana; (15) 2009 Sharm el-Sheikh; (16) 2012 Tehran; (17) 2016 Isla de Margarita Venezuela; (18) 2019 Baku; (19) 2024 KAMPALA Uganda. INDIA (under Modi) HAS SKIPPED 4 recent NAM summits (2016, 2019, 2024 — sent Vice President; 2016 was 1st ever Indian PM to miss). CRITIQUES: (a) Cold War ended 1991 — what's NAM's relevance? (b) 'NON-alignment' replaced by 'MULTI-alignment' in India's strategic language (S Jaishankar). (c) Internal contradictions — mixed regimes, conflicting interests (e.g., India vs China both joined; Pakistan member; Iran-Saudi-Iraq-Israel; Cuba-USA). (d) Forum of discussion more than action body. DEFENCE of NAM: (a) Represents developing world / Global South collective voice. (b) UN reform push. (c) South-South cooperation. (d) Anti-sanctions (Cuba, Iran, Venezuela). (e) Climate justice + SDGs + debt reform. INDIA's EVOLVING POSITION: (a) Nehruvian non-alignment ideology. (b) Post-1991 economic reforms + rapprochement with USA. (c) Post-2014 Modi + Jaishankar doctrine: 'INDIA will engage with all, align with none' — effectively 'strategic autonomy' + 'multi-alignment' (BRICS + Quad + SCO + G20 + BIMSTEC + NAM + bilaterals all active). (d) De-prioritisation of NAM optics without formal exit. by NEHRU (India) + TITO (Yugoslavia) + NASSER (Egypt) + SUKARNO (Indonesia) + NKRUMAH (Ghana); 120 current members.

cards.front:
The ASEAN (Association of South-East Asian Nations) has how many member states?

(A) 6
(B) 10
(C) 15
(D) 3
cards.back:
(B) 10

International & Organizations — ASEAN (ASSOCIATION of SOUTH-EAST ASIAN NATIONS) — major regional organisation of SE Asian countries. FOUNDED 8 August 1967 via BANGKOK DECLARATION signed by 5 FOUNDING MEMBERS: INDONESIA + MALAYSIA + PHILIPPINES + SINGAPORE + THAILAND. Subsequent expansions: BRUNEI (1984, after independence from UK), VIETNAM (1995, post normalisation), LAOS + MYANMAR (1997), CAMBODIA (1999). Now 10 MEMBERS. TIMOR-LESTE (East Timor) — 11th — admitted 'in principle' 2022, full member targeted by 2025 (observer now). HQ: JAKARTA (Indonesia). TOTAL POP: ~700 million (~8% world). Combined GDP ~$3.6 trillion (5th largest economy bloc). CHARTER adopted 2007 (ratified 2008). OBJECTIVES: (1) Economic growth + social progress + cultural development. (2) Peace + security. (3) Collaboration + mutual assistance. (4) Multi-lateral Cooperation. (5) Respect sovereignty + non-interference + peaceful dispute resolution. ASEAN WAY — consensus-based + non-interference + quiet diplomacy; criticised for softness on Myanmar junta + human rights issues. ASEAN SUMMITS: ANNUAL — 2 meetings per year (ASEAN Summit in November + ASEAN Regional Forum ARF in July; also ASEAN+3, East Asia Summit EAS, RCEP). CHAIRMANSHIP ROTATES alphabetically. 2024 — LAOS; 2025 — MALAYSIA; 2026 — PHILIPPINES. IMPORTANCE of ASEAN: (a) High growth + integration model for developing regions; (b) CENTRAL role in Indo-Pacific architecture — most frameworks 'ASEAN-centric' (Quad + EAS + RCEP); (c) Largest trading partner of CHINA + 3rd partner of USA + INDIA; (d) ASEAN-INDIA FTA (2009 signed, 2010 in force); (e) Major recipient of FDI. KEY MECHANISMS: (1) AFTA (ASEAN Free Trade Area, 1992). (2) ASEAN ECONOMIC COMMUNITY (AEC, 2015) — single market + production base. (3) RCEP (Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership) — world's LARGEST trade deal; 15 members (ASEAN 10 + China + Japan + S Korea + Australia + NZ); signed 2020, in force Jan 2022. India WITHDREW 2019 (Modi govt) citing deficit concerns + China dominance + agri concerns. (4) ASEAN+1, +3 (with China, Japan, S Korea), +6. (5) East Asia Summit (EAS, 2005, 18 members including India + USA). (6) ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF, 1994) — 27 members incl USA, China, EU. (7) ASEAN Defence Ministers Meeting Plus (ADMM+). (8) ACT EAST POLICY — India's engagement (from Look East Policy 1991 Narasimha Rao, renamed 2014 by Modi); annual summits with ASEAN since 2002; CEPA agreements; infrastructure (Kaladan multi-modal Myanmar-Mizoram transit, India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway). ASEAN CHALLENGES: (1) SOUTH CHINA SEA disputes — China's 'Nine-Dash Line' claim vs Vietnam, Philippines, Malaysia, Brunei, Taiwan. UNCLOS arbitration 2016 favoured Philippines; China rejected. Artificial islands militarised. (2) MYANMAR coup Feb 2021 — ASEAN's '5-Point Consensus' ineffective; junta atrocities continue. (3) Mekong River water stresses (Chinese upstream dams). (4) Climate change (IPCC most-vulnerable region). INDIA's ACT EAST: (a) Strategic — maritime security, Quad synergy. (b) Economic — RCEP withdrawal setback but bilateral + mini-lateral engagement (India-ASEAN, I-Japan, I-Vietnam, I-Indonesia). (c) Cultural — Ramayana routes, Buddhism diplomacy. (d) North East connectivity — Myanmar, Thailand. INDIA aims at Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI 2019) + SAGAR (Security + Growth for All in the Region, 2015 Maritime doctrine). Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand (1967 founders) + Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Cambodia (later); TIMOR-LESTE 11th pending 2025.

cards.front:
The WORLD TRADE ORGANIZATION (WTO) was established in:

(A) 1947
(B) 1 January 1995
(C) 2001 Doha
(D) 1960
cards.back:
(B) 1 January 1995

International & Organizations — WTO (WORLD TRADE ORGANIZATION) — only GLOBAL international ORG dealing with RULES of trade between nations. ESTABLISHED 1 JANUARY 1995 (Marrakesh Agreement 1994). HQ: GENEVA, Switzerland. 164 MEMBER STATES (as of 2024) + 22 observers. INDIA is FOUNDING member. PREDECESSOR: GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs + Trade) — 1947-1994; provisional body signed by 23 countries after UN failure to form International Trade Organization (US Senate rejected ITO Charter 1950). GATT held 8 'ROUNDS' of trade negotiations; successive tariff cuts. URUGUAY ROUND (1986-94) culminated in WTO's creation + broadened scope (services, IP, investment, agriculture, textiles). FUNCTIONS of WTO: (1) Administer TRADE AGREEMENTS. (2) FORUM for trade negotiations. (3) Settle TRADE DISPUTES (DSB — Dispute Settlement Body; WTO's 'crown jewel' though stressed since 2019 by US blocking AB appointments). (4) MONITOR national trade policies (via Trade Policy Review). (5) TECHNICAL assistance + training for developing countries. (6) COOPERATE with IMF + World Bank. STRUCTURE: (a) MINISTERIAL CONFERENCE (MC) — highest body; meets every 2 years. MC-1 Singapore 1996; MC-13 Abu Dhabi Feb-Mar 2024 (latest). (b) GENERAL COUNCIL — day-to-day; meets in Geneva. (c) COUNCILS for GOODS (CTG), SERVICES (CTS), TRIPS. (d) DIRECTOR-GENERAL — 4-year term. Current DG: NGOZI OKONJO-IWEALA (Nigeria, since Mar 2021, second term 2025-29 announced Dec 2024) — FIRST WOMAN + FIRST AFRICAN DG. Prior: Ronaldo Azevêdo (Brazil 2013-20). PRINCIPLES of WTO: (1) NON-DISCRIMINATION — (a) MFN (Most Favoured Nation) — treat all WTO members equally; (b) NATIONAL TREATMENT — domestic + foreign products/services treated alike. (2) Freer trade via negotiation. (3) Predictability via bindings + transparency. (4) Promoting fair competition. (5) Encouraging development + economic reform. KEY AGREEMENTS: (1) GATT — goods. (2) GATS — services. (3) TRIPS (Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights) — patents + copyrights + trademarks. (4) TRIMS (Trade-Related Investment Measures). (5) ANTI-DUMPING, SUBSIDIES + Countervailing, Safeguards agreements. (6) AGREEMENT ON AGRICULTURE (AOA) — liberalising farm trade. (7) SPS (Sanitary + Phytosanitary Measures). (8) TBT (Technical Barriers to Trade). (9) Textiles Agreement (MFA phased out 2005). NEGOTIATION ROUNDS (WTO era): (a) DOHA ROUND / DOHA DEVELOPMENT AGENDA (launched Nov 2001, Qatar) — focused on developing countries' interests; STALLED since mid-2000s due to N-S disputes (agri subsidies, non-agri market access); effectively stuck. (b) BALI PACKAGE 2013 — trade facilitation. (c) Nairobi Package 2015. (d) Geneva Package 2022. (e) Abu Dhabi MC-13 (Feb-Mar 2024) — renewed moratorium on e-commerce customs duties (key for India + African states); TRIPS fisheries; but NO big breakthroughs. INDIA's CONCERNS at WTO: (1) PSH (Public Stockholding for Food Security) — INDIA's MSP + NFSA considered 'trade-distorting' subsidies under AOA; India has permanent 'peace clause' (Bali) but WANTS lasting solution. (2) Fisheries subsidies — India blocked agreements in 2022 protecting fishermen's livelihoods. (3) Digital trade — wants 'more development-friendly' terms. (4) Agriculture — DIFF between developed + developing 'special + differential treatment' not strong enough. (5) Use WTO DSB selectively — INDIA won key US steel + solar cases. DSB APPELLATE BODY — paralysed since 2019 (Trump blocking member appointments; Biden continued); 'multi-party interim appeal arrangement' (MPIA) alternative with 26 countries; USA still blocks. WTO reform critical for rule-based trade. DOHA Declaration on TRIPS + Public Health (2001) allows COMPULSORY LICENSING of drugs in health emergencies (India pioneered via Bayer Nexavar 2012, Gilead Sovaldi). successor to GATT (1947); HQ Geneva; 164 member states; INDIA founding member; Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala current DG (Nigeria).

cards.front:
The INTERNATIONAL MONETARY FUND (IMF) + WORLD BANK were established at:

(A) Yalta Conference 1945
(B) BRETTON WOODS CONFERENCE 1944
(C) Paris Treaty 1947
(D) Tokyo Round
cards.back:
(B) BRETTON WOODS CONFERENCE 1944

International & Organizations — BRETTON WOODS CONFERENCE (UN Monetary + Financial Conference) — 1-22 JULY 1944 at Mount Washington Hotel, BRETTON WOODS, NEW HAMPSHIRE, USA. 730 delegates from 44 ALLIED nations (still WWII — before Germany's surrender May 1945). Goal: plan POSTWAR GLOBAL economic order. Co-chaired by (1) JOHN MAYNARD KEYNES (UK) — proposed 'International Clearing Union' + bancor supranational currency (not adopted); and (2) HARRY DEXTER WHITE (USA) — whose plan largely adopted. RESULTS: (1) IMF (INTERNATIONAL MONETARY FUND) — formal establishment Dec 1945; began operations 1 March 1947. HQ: WASHINGTON DC. MANDATE: promote international monetary cooperation; exchange rate stability; BoP financing for members in crisis. 191 member states. (2) IBRD (International Bank for Reconstruction + Development) — 'ORIGINAL World Bank'; began 1946. For Europe's post-WWII reconstruction + developing countries. Expanded to become WORLD BANK GROUP. (3) BRETTON WOODS SYSTEM of FIXED EXCHANGE RATES — currencies pegged to US DOLLAR, which was pegged to GOLD at $35/oz. Central banks could exchange USD for gold. Ended 15 Aug 1971 when Nixon 'CLOSED THE GOLD WINDOW' (Nixon Shock) due to dollar overhang. Since 1973 — mostly floating exchange rates. IMF STRUCTURE: (1) Board of Governors — ministers of finance / central bank governors from each member. (2) EXECUTIVE BOARD — 24 members, daily operations; US + UK + Japan + Germany + France + China each have own director; others grouped. (3) MANAGING DIRECTOR — 5-year term; by CONVENTION from EUROPE (while WB president from USA — 'gentlemen's agreement'). Current: KRISTALINA GEORGIEVA (Bulgaria, since Oct 2019, 2nd term from 2024). Past: Christine Lagarde (France 2011-19, now ECB Chief), Dominique Strauss-Kahn (France 2007-11). (4) Chief Economist — currently Pierre-Olivier Gourinchas (France). Past: Raghuram Rajan (India, 2003-06 — youngest ever; later RBI Governor 2013-16); Gita Gopinath (Indian-American 2019-22, first woman + first Indian). Indira Gandhi's 1966 devaluation was IMF-mandated. QUOTAS + VOTING: members' contributions (based on GDP + economic openness) determine votes. USA ~17% votes = de facto VETO (since major decisions need 85%). CHINA recently rose to 3rd largest quota share. India is 8th; 2019 reforms slightly increased developing countries' weights. SPECIAL DRAWING RIGHTS (SDR) — IMF's RESERVE ASSET since 1969. Basket of 5 currencies (USD + EUR + JPY + GBP + RMB added 2016). Issued occasionally (largest $650 BILLION in Aug 2021 to fight COVID). Members can exchange SDRs for hard currency. FUNCTIONS: (a) SURVEILLANCE — Article IV consultations (annual assessment of each country). (b) LENDING — BoP crises; conditional loans (controversial); 'Stand-By Arrangements', Extended Fund Facility. (c) Technical Assistance. KEY IMF CRISIS INTERVENTIONS: (1) 1970s-80s LATIN AMERICA debt crisis; (2) 1990s ASIAN Financial Crisis (IMF austerity controversial; 'IMF riots'); (3) 1991 INDIA BoP crisis — IMF + WB loans + conditionality catalysed LPG REFORMS (Narasimha Rao + Manmohan Singh). (4) 1997 Korea, Thailand, Indonesia; (5) 2001 Argentina; (6) 2008 GREECE Eurozone crisis; (7) 2010-18 BAILOUTS in Europe. (8) SRI LANKA 2022 default — IMF $3B package 2023-24. (9) PAKISTAN recurrent packages. (10) COVID-19 response — massive support to ~90 countries. WORLD BANK GROUP: (1) IBRD (1944/46) — middle-income + creditworthy low-income. (2) IDA (International Development Association, 1960) — poorest countries; interest-free loans + grants. (3) IFC (Int Financial Corp, 1956) — private sector. (4) MIGA (Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, 1988) — political risk insurance. (5) ICSID (1965) — investment disputes settlement. Current WB PRESIDENT: AJAY BANGA (Indian-American, since June 2023) — first Indian-origin + first person of color to head WB. attended by 44 nations; 'Bretton Woods System' fixed exchange rates tied to gold + USD; collapsed 1971; New Hampshire, USA.

RESULTS: (1) IMF (INTERNATIONAL MONETARY FUND) — formal establishment Dec 1945; began operations 1 March 1947. HQ: WASHINGTON DC. MANDATE: promote international monetary cooperation; exchange rate stability; BoP financing for members in crisis. 191 member states. (2) IBRD (International Bank for Reconstruction + Development) — 'ORIGINAL World Bank'; began 1946. For Europe's post-WWII reconstruction + developing countries. Expanded to become WORLD BANK GROUP. (3) BRETTON WOODS SYSTEM of FIXED EXCHANGE RATES — currencies pegged to US DOLLAR, which was pegged to GOLD at $35/oz. Central banks could exchange USD for gold. Ended 15 Aug 1971 when Nixon 'CLOSED THE GOLD WINDOW' (Nixon Shock) due to dollar overhang. Since 1973 — mostly floating exchange rates. IMF STRUCTURE: (1) Board of Governors — ministers of finance / central bank governors from each member. (2) EXECUTIVE BOARD — 24 members, daily operations; US + UK + Japan + Germany + France + China each have own director; others grouped. (3) MANAGING DIRECTOR — 5-year term; by CONVENTION from EUROPE (while WB president from USA — 'gentlemen's agreement'). Current: KRISTALINA GEORGIEVA (Bulgaria, since Oct 2019, 2nd term from 2024). Past: Christine Lagarde (France 2011-19, now ECB Chief), Dominique Strauss-Kahn (France 2007-11). (4) Chief Economist — currently Pierre-Olivier Gourinchas (France). Past: Raghuram Rajan (India, 2003-06 — youngest ever; later RBI Governor 2013-16); Gita Gopinath (Indian-American 2019-22, first woman + first Indian). Indira Gandhi's 1966 devaluation was IMF-mandated. QUOTAS + VOTING: members' contributions (based on GDP + economic openness) determine votes. USA ~17% votes = de facto VETO (since major decisions need 85%). CHINA recently rose to 3rd largest quota share. India is 8th; 2019 reforms slightly increased developing countries' weights. SPECIAL DRAWING RIGHTS (SDR) — IMF's RESERVE ASSET since 1969. Basket of 5 currencies (USD + EUR + JPY + GBP + RMB added 2016). Issued occasionally (largest $650 BILLION in Aug 2021 to fight COVID). Members can exchange SDRs for hard currency. FUNCTIONS: (a) SURVEILLANCE — Article IV consultations (annual assessment of each country). (b) LENDING — BoP crises; conditional loans (controversial); 'Stand-By Arrangements', Extended Fund Facility. (c) Technical Assistance. KEY IMF CRISIS INTERVENTIONS: (1) 1970s-80s LATIN AMERICA debt crisis; (2) 1990s ASIAN Financial Crisis (IMF austerity controversial; 'IMF riots'); (3) 1991 INDIA BoP crisis — IMF + WB loans + conditionality catalysed LPG REFORMS (Narasimha Rao + Manmohan Singh). (4) 1997 Korea, Thailand, Indonesia; (5) 2001 Argentina; (6) 2008 GREECE Eurozone crisis; (7) 2010-18 BAILOUTS in Europe. (8) SRI LANKA 2022 default — IMF $3B package 2023-24. (9) PAKISTAN recurrent packages. (10) COVID-19 response — massive support to ~90 countries. WORLD BANK GROUP: (1) IBRD (1944/46) — middle-income + creditworthy low-income. (2) IDA (International Development Association, 1960) — poorest countries; interest-free loans + grants. (3) IFC (Int Financial Corp, 1956) — private sector. (4) MIGA (Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, 1988) — political risk insurance. (5) ICSID (1965) — investment disputes settlement. Current WB PRESIDENT: AJAY BANGA (Indian-American, since June 2023) — first Indian-origin + first person of color to head WB. attended by 44 nations; 'Bretton Woods System' fixed exchange rates tied to gold + USD; collapsed 1971; New Hampshire, USA.

cards.front:
The SHANGHAI COOPERATION ORGANISATION (SCO) has how many full member states (2024)?

(A) 5
(B) 10
(C) 3
(D) 20
cards.back:
(B) 10

International & Organizations — SCO (SHANGHAI COOPERATION ORGANISATION) — Eurasian political + economic + security organisation. FOUNDED 15 JUNE 2001 at SHANGHAI. Evolved from SHANGHAI FIVE (1996) — China + Russia + Kazakhstan + Kyrgyzstan + Tajikistan. Uzbekistan joined 2001 → SCO-6. India + Pakistan 2017 → SCO-8. Iran 2023 → SCO-9. Belarus 9 Jun 2024 → SCO-10. Current 10 members. OBSERVER states: Afghanistan, Mongolia. Dialogue partners: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bahrain, Cambodia, Egypt, Kuwait, Maldives, Myanmar, Nepal, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Sri Lanka, Turkey, UAE. HQ: BEIJING (secretariat); REGIONAL ANTI-TERRORIST STRUCTURE (RATS) at TASHKENT Uzbekistan. Official languages: RUSSIAN + CHINESE (no English — reflects non-Western orientation). CURRENT SCO CAPACITY: ~40% of global population + ~30% of GDP + ~70% of Eurasian landmass. OBJECTIVES (Shanghai Convention): (1) Strengthen MUTUAL TRUST + neighbourhood + friendship. (2) Encourage COOPERATION in politics, trade, economy, scientific, technology, culture, education, energy, transport + environment. (3) JOINT EFFORTS to maintain peace + security + stability in region. (4) COMBAT 'THREE EVILS' — TERRORISM + SEPARATISM + EXTREMISM. Anti-terror focus pronounced. SCO SUMMITS: ANNUAL Heads-of-State Summit + Heads-of-Government Summit. Chair rotates. Recent: (1) 2022 SAMARKAND Uzbekistan — Iran admitted; Putin attended despite Ukraine war; Modi met Xi first time. (2) 2023 NEW DELHI (India's 1st SCO Summit; held VIRTUAL; India's downgrading amid LAC tensions with China). (3) 2024 ASTANA Kazakhstan — Modi SKIPPED (sent S. Jaishankar); Belarus admitted. (4) 2025 TIANJIN (China). INDIA's SCO dynamics: (1) Joined 2017 (Kazakhstan) along with Pakistan — expected to lead to increased Indo-Pak dialogue; hasn't materialised — 2023 Jaishankar-Bhutto meeting was rare exchange. (2) India's dilemma — SCO is CHINA + RUSSIA dominated; counter-Western; India's strategic autonomy strategy participates but doesn't commit to anti-West rhetoric. (3) RATS cooperation on terrorism useful (intel sharing). (4) Central Asia access — potential for INSTC (International North-South Transport Corridor; India-Iran-Russia route bypassing Pakistan; 15-year stagnation, recent progress with Chabahar port operation 2024). (5) China-India LAC tensions Galwan 2020 cooled enthusiasm. ISSUES: (1) CHINA-INDIA rivalry, LAC border, BRI vs IMEC. (2) India-Pakistan hostility — rare SCO dialogue. (3) Russia's Ukraine war (Feb 2022-) divides members; India abstained at UN votes; doesn't subscribe to 'West'. (4) Iran's admission politicised. (5) AFGHANISTAN situation (Taliban since Aug 2021) — SCO discussions. COMPETITIVE GROUPINGS: (a) NATO (32 members since Sweden 2024). (b) EU (27 members). (c) EAEU (Eurasian Economic Union — Russia + Belarus + Kazakhstan + Armenia + Kyrgyzstan). (d) CSTO (Collective Security Treaty Organisation — 6 members; Russia-led military). (e) QUAD. (f) BRICS+. MULTI-ALIGNMENT is new normal for INDIA: QUAD (USA + Japan + Australia) + SCO (China + Russia) + BRICS (Russia + China + Brazil + S Africa) + G20 + NAM + IBSA + I2U2. S. Jaishankar's doctrine of 'friends of friends, partners of partners'. India's foreign policy = strategic autonomy + issue-based alignment + multi-engagement. original China, Russia + Kazakhstan + Kyrgyzstan + Tajikistan + Uzbekistan; INDIA + PAKISTAN joined 2017; IRAN 2023; BELARUS 2024 (10th).

cards.front:
OPEC (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries) was founded in:

(A) 1947
(B) 1960 at Baghdad
(C) 1995
(D) 1985
cards.back:
(B) 1960 at Baghdad

International & Organizations — OPEC (ORGANIZATION OF THE PETROLEUM EXPORTING COUNTRIES) — cartel of oil-producing nations; controls ~40% of world oil + ~80% proven reserves. FOUNDED 10-14 SEPT 1960 at BAGHDAD CONFERENCE by 5 FOUNDING MEMBERS: IRAN, IRAQ, KUWAIT, SAUDI ARABIA, VENEZUELA. HQ originally GENEVA 1961-65; moved to VIENNA Austria 1965. OBJECTIVES: (1) Coordinate + unify oil policies of members for fair + stable prices. (2) EFFICIENT, economic + regular supply to consumers. (3) Fair return on capital for producers. CURRENT 12 MEMBERS (2024): Algeria, Angola (joined 2007, left Jan 2024), Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Libya, Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Venezuela. Some left over years: Indonesia (suspended 2008, left 2016), Qatar (left 2019), Angola (left 2024). ECUADOR + Indonesia had also joined + left. OPEC+ — in 2016, OPEC formed alliance with 10 non-OPEC producers led by RUSSIA = 23 countries (10 OPEC + 13 non-OPEC). Russia + Kazakhstan + Mexico + Azerbaijan + Oman + Bahrain + Brunei + Malaysia + Sudan + South Sudan. Collectively control ~55-60% of world oil. Meets regularly to set production quotas. DECISIONS + HISTORY: (1) 1973 OIL EMBARGO — OPEC Arab states (OAPEC) banned oil exports to USA + others over Yom Kippur War support of Israel. Oil price quadrupled ($3 → $12/barrel); global recession; US 55 mph speed limit + daylight savings changes; Indian BoP squeeze. Shift of power to oil exporters. (2) 1979-80 — Iranian Revolution + Iran-Iraq War → oil SHOCK-2 ($40/barrel). (3) 1986 — Oil price crash. (4) 1990-91 — Gulf War supply disruption. (5) 2008 — oil hit $147/barrel (all-time high) then crashed in global financial crisis. (6) 2014-16 — SHALE REVOLUTION in USA + oversupply → oil crashed from $110 to $30. (7) 2016 — Saudi + Russia 'OPEC+' deal formalised production cuts. (8) March 2020 — COVID-19 demand collapse; Saudi-Russia price war; oil futures went NEGATIVE (-$37) in April 2020 (first time ever) due to storage lack. (9) 2022 — Ukraine invasion; Russia oil sanctions; G7 price cap $60/barrel on Russian oil (Dec 2022). (10) 2023-24 — OPEC+ cutting production (3-5 M barrels/day) to support prices; Saudi + UAE tensions; Saudi Aramco IPO (largest ever). (11) 2024 — Angola EXITED over quota disputes. (12) OPEC MONTHLY OIL MARKET REPORT (MOMR). SAUDI ARAMCO — world's MOST VALUABLE company sometimes; Crown Prince MBS (Mohammed bin Salman) + Vision 2030 diversification drive (NEOM megacity, entertainment, tourism). WORLD OIL STATS (2024): (1) PRODUCTION — USA #1 (~13 M b/d, shale surged since 2008); Saudi #2 (~10 M); Russia #3 (~9-10 M); Canada 4th; Iraq + UAE + Brazil + Iran. (2) RESERVES — VENEZUELA #1 proven (300B barrels, much heavy), Saudi #2, Iran, Canada (oil sands), Iraq, UAE, Kuwait, Russia, Libya, Nigeria. (3) CONSUMPTION — USA #1, China #2, India #3, Japan, Russia, Germany, Brazil. (4) IMPORTS — China #1, Europe, India. Indian dependence ~85% on imports. (5) INDIA's TOP OIL SUPPLIERS: Iraq, Saudi, UAE, Russia (post 2022 discounted), USA, Nigeria. Russia replaced Iraq as top supplier 2023. INDIAN OIL CRISIS CONTEXT: 1991 BoP crisis partly from Gulf War oil spike. Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) — Vizag, Mangaluru, Padur; adding more. Future: (1) Renewables replacing oil (EVs, solar); (2) peak oil demand projected 2030; (3) Gulf states diversifying economies; (4) green hydrogen as oil alternative. 5 founders (Iran + Iraq + Kuwait + Saudi Arabia + Venezuela); 12 current members; HQ Vienna since 1965; 1973 oil embargo + 2016 'OPEC+' with Russia.

The ONLY ancient Wonder of the World still standing today is:

(A) Colossus of Rhodes
(B) Great Pyramid of Giza (Egypt)
(C) Hanging Gardens of Babylon
(D) Lighthouse of Alexandria
cards.back:
(B) Great Pyramid of Giza (Egypt)

(A) Olympics 1900
(B) 1889 Paris World's Fair
(C) D-Day commemoration

cards.back:

Made of iron, ~10,100 tonnes. centennial of French Revolution.

cards.front:
The CENTRAL PROCESSING UNIT (CPU) of a computer is called the:

(A) Memory of the computer
(B) BRAIN of the computer
(C) Output device
(D) Data storage
cards.back:
(B) BRAIN of the computer

Science, Tech & Defence — CPU (CENTRAL PROCESSING UNIT) — 'BRAIN OF THE COMPUTER'; executes instructions of computer programs (fetching from memory, decoding, executing, writing back). ALSO called PROCESSOR / microprocessor. INTERNAL COMPONENTS: (1) ARITHMETIC LOGIC UNIT (ALU) — performs arithmetic (+, −, ×, ÷) + logic (AND, OR, NOT, XOR, comparisons) operations. (2) CONTROL UNIT (CU) — directs flow of data + instructions; decodes instructions + signals ALU + memory + I/O. (3) REGISTERS — small fast storage inside CPU (general-purpose, instruction register, program counter, stack pointer, etc.). (4) CACHE MEMORY — ultra-fast SRAM close to CPU (L1, L2, L3 levels); reduces RAM access latency. CPU METRICS: (a) CLOCK SPEED (in GHz — billions of cycles per second; modern CPUs 3-5 GHz). (b) CORES (independent execution units; modern CPUs 4-64+ cores; server CPUs like AMD EPYC 9654 = 96 cores). (c) THREADS (1-2 per core; Intel Hyper-Threading / AMD SMT). (d) CACHE size (L1 ~64KB/core, L2 512KB-1MB, L3 many MB shared). (e) IPC (Instructions Per Clock). CPU MANUFACTURERS: (1) INTEL — market leader for decades; x86 architecture; Core i3/i5/i7/i9, Xeon (server); recent struggles vs AMD. (2) AMD — Ryzen (desktop/laptop), EPYC (server), Threadripper (workstation); strong comeback since Zen arch 2017. (3) APPLE — M1/M2/M3/M4 ARM-based silicon (2020 onwards) — revolutionised Macbook + iPad; also iPhone A-series. (4) QUALCOMM — Snapdragon for mobile (Android); recently Snapdragon X Elite for PCs. (5) ARM Holdings (UK/Japan-owned) — licenses ARM architecture; most smartphones worldwide. (6) MediaTek, Samsung Exynos, HiSilicon Kirin. INSTRUCTION SET ARCHITECTURES (ISA): x86 (Intel + AMD — CISC), ARM (mobile + Apple Silicon + Snapdragon PCs — RISC), RISC-V (open-source, rising), PowerPC (niche). TRANSISTOR COUNT: Moore's Law — doubling every 2 years (Gordon Moore, Intel, 1965). Current top CPUs have 100+ BILLION transistors. PROCESS NODE: 3nm (TSMC N3 for Apple M3 + Snapdragon 8 Gen 3), 4nm (mass), 2nm coming (Intel 18A, TSMC N2). INDIAN CPU: (a) SHAKTI (IIT Madras) — open-source RISC-V family; 'Made in India'. (b) AJIT (IIT Bombay) — low-power. Semiconductor manufacturing drive: IndiaSemicon policy 2022; Micron, Vedanta-Foxconn, Tata-PSMC fabs in Gujarat + TN; India Semiconductor Mission (ISM). executes instructions; has ARITHMETIC LOGIC UNIT (ALU) + CONTROL UNIT (CU) + REGISTERS.

cards.front:
The SMALLEST unit of data in a computer is a:

(A) Byte
(B) BIT
(C) Nibble
(D) Word
cards.back:
(B) BIT

Science, Tech & Defence — COMPUTER DATA UNITS HIERARCHY: (1) BIT (Binary digIT) — smallest unit; value 0 or 1 (OFF/ON, False/True). Named by Claude Shannon (1948) + John Tukey. (2) NIBBLE — 4 bits (half byte; one hex digit). (3) BYTE — 8 BITS; basic addressable unit in most computers; can represent 256 values (0-255); one ASCII character or a small integer. (4) KILOBYTE (KB) — 1,024 bytes (binary) or 1,000 bytes (decimal, SI; technically KiB for binary per IEC). (5) MEGABYTE (MB) — 1,024 KB ≈ 10⁶ B. (6) GIGABYTE (GB) — 1,024 MB ≈ 10⁹ B. (7) TERABYTE (TB) — 10¹² B. (8) PETABYTE (PB) — 10¹⁵ B. (9) EXABYTE (EB) — 10¹⁸. (10) ZETTABYTE (ZB) — 10²¹. (11) YOTTABYTE (YB) — 10²⁴. Global digital data: ~180 ZB annually (2025). REFERENCE sizes: (a) MP3 song ~5 MB. (b) 1-hour HD video ~4 GB. (c) 4K movie ~25 GB. (d) Modern SSDs 500GB-8TB; cloud storage PB. (e) Library of Congress digitized ~10 PB. NUMBER REPRESENTATION: (1) BINARY (base 2) — computer native; 0, 1. (2) OCTAL (base 8). (3) DECIMAL (base 10, human). (4) HEXADECIMAL (base 16) — compact display of bytes; 00 to FF per byte; uses 0-9, A-F. CHARACTER ENCODING: (1) ASCII — 7-bit; 128 characters (English); 1960s. (2) EXTENDED ASCII — 8-bit; 256. (3) UNICODE — universal; 1,100,000+ characters covering all world scripts (English, Devanagari, Chinese, Arabic, Emoji etc.). Encodings: UTF-8 (1-4 bytes, most common on web, 95%+ of pages), UTF-16, UTF-32. EMOJI — over 3,000 Unicode code points. DATA vs INFORMATION: DATA = raw facts/figures; INFORMATION = processed, organised, meaningful data. STORAGE TYPES: (1) PRIMARY (volatile) — RAM, CPU registers, Cache; very fast, lost when power off. (2) SECONDARY (non-volatile) — HDD, SSD, SD cards, USB drives, optical (CD/DVD/Blu-ray); persistent. (3) TERTIARY — archival, tape (LTO magnetic), optical libraries, cloud glacier storage. COMMON FILE SIZES: text 1-10 KB/page; image 100 KB-10 MB; audio 1-10 MB/min; video 10 MB-1 GB/min. DATA COMPRESSION: LOSSLESS (ZIP, PNG, FLAC) + LOSSY (JPEG, MP3, H.264, AAC) — lossy throws away info not noticed by humans. 0 or 1; 8 bits = 1 BYTE; memory + storage typically measured in bytes (KB, MB, GB, TB, PB); Binary Digit.

cards.front:
The FATHER OF COMPUTER is considered to be:

(A) Bill Gates
(B) CHARLES BABBAGE (1791-1871)
(C) Alan Turing
(D) Herman Hollerith
cards.back:
(B) CHARLES BABBAGE (1791-1871)

Science, Tech & Defence — CHARLES BABBAGE (1791-1871) — English polymath; widely regarded as the 'FATHER OF COMPUTER'. DESIGNED (though never fully built in his lifetime): (1) DIFFERENCE ENGINE (started 1822) — mechanical calculator for polynomial functions + generating mathematical tables automatically; handled by cranks + gears; partially built, abandoned. RECONSTRUCTED by Science Museum London (1991-2002) from Babbage's drawings — IT WORKED! (2) ANALYTICAL ENGINE (designed 1837) — proposed general-purpose MECHANICAL COMPUTER with separate 'store' (memory), 'mill' (CPU), punched-card INPUT (inspired by Jacquard loom), conditional branching, loops. All concepts of MODERN COMPUTER architecturally anticipated! Never built. ADA LOVELACE (1815-1852, daughter of Lord Byron) — Babbage's collaborator; wrote the FIRST ALGORITHM intended for a machine (Bernoulli numbers computation for Analytical Engine). Considered 'WORLD's FIRST COMPUTER PROGRAMMER'. October celebrates 'Ada Lovelace Day'. Programming language ADA (US DoD 1983) named after her. OTHER COMPUTING PIONEERS: (1) BLAISE PASCAL (1642) — Pascaline mechanical calculator (addition). (2) GOTTFRIED LEIBNIZ (1673) — Stepped Reckoner (×/÷); invented binary number system + concept of calculus ratiocinator. (3) GEORGE BOOLE (1854) — Boolean algebra (basis of digital logic). (4) HERMAN HOLLERITH (1890) — punched card tabulator for US 1890 Census → founded Tabulating Machine Company → merged into IBM (1911, renamed 1924). (5) ALAN TURING (1912-54) — CONCEPTUAL basis of computability; TURING MACHINE (1936); broke Enigma at Bletchley Park WWII; Turing test for AI (1950); Turing Award = 'Nobel of computing'. (6) KONRAD ZUSE (1938-41) — Z1, Z3 (first programmable digital computer, Germany). (7) JOHN ATANASOFF + CLIFFORD BERRY (1942) — ABC (first electronic digital computer). (8) JOHN MAUCHLY + J.P. ECKERT (1946) — ENIAC (Electronic Numerical Integrator + Computer; 18,000 vacuum tubes; US Army Ballistic Research Lab). Often called first general-purpose electronic computer. (9) JOHN von NEUMANN (1945) — von Neumann architecture (shared memory for data + programs) — basis of modern computers. (10) GRACE HOPPER — FLOW-MATIC + COBOL; coined 'debug' when moth found in relay. EDSAC (1949, UK, Maurice Wilkes), EDVAC, MANCHESTER Mark 1. FIRST COMMERCIAL computer = UNIVAC 1 (1951). India's first computer = HEC-2M (Calcutta, 1955 via HOMI BHABHA, imported British). First Indian-designed = TIFRAC (1960 Bombay, by TIFR). Param Siddhi-AI (2020) = India's fastest supercomputer. English mathematician; designed 'DIFFERENCE ENGINE' (1822) + 'ANALYTICAL ENGINE' (1837); first programmable computer concept.

India's first computer = HEC-2M (Calcutta, 1955 via HOMI BHABHA, imported British). First Indian-designed = TIFRAC (1960 Bombay, by TIFR). Param Siddhi-AI (2020) = India's fastest supercomputer. English mathematician; designed 'DIFFERENCE ENGINE' (1822) + 'ANALYTICAL ENGINE' (1837); first programmable computer concept.

cards.front:
RAM (Random Access Memory) is:

(A) Permanent storage
(B) VOLATILE (temporary) memory
(C) Disk-based
(D) Only read-only
cards.back:
(B) VOLATILE (temporary) memory

Science, Tech & Defence — RAM (RANDOM ACCESS MEMORY) — PRIMARY storage for running programs + data in use. Called 'random access' because ANY location can be accessed directly in the same time (unlike sequential access tape). CHARACTERISTICS: (1) VOLATILE — LOSES DATA when power removed; 'working memory' of computer. (2) FAST — 10-100x faster than SSD, 1000x faster than HDD. (3) EXPENSIVE per GB than disk. TYPES: (1) DRAM (Dynamic RAM) — modern main memory; uses capacitor + transistor per bit; needs REFRESHING (capacitor discharges). Standards: DDR3 (2007), DDR4 (2014), DDR5 (2020-, current). LPDDR (low-power) for mobile; GDDR for graphics cards. (2) SRAM (Static RAM) — 6 transistors per bit; FASTER but more expensive; used for CPU CACHE (L1/L2/L3). Doesn't need refresh. TYPICAL RAM sizes (2024): mobile 4-16 GB; budget laptop 8 GB; mainstream 16 GB; gaming/creator 32 GB; workstation 64-256 GB; server 256GB-24TB. ROM (READ-ONLY MEMORY) — NON-VOLATILE; stores BIOS/UEFI firmware (boot code), embedded system software. TYPES: (1) PROM (programmable once); (2) EPROM (erasable via UV); (3) EEPROM (electrically erasable); (4) FLASH memory (modern, block-erased; SSDs + USB drives + SD cards based on NAND flash). STORAGE: (1) HDD (Hard Disk Drive) — spinning magnetic platters; slow (mechanical); 100-250 MB/s; cheap; typical 1-20 TB. Seagate, WD. (2) SSD (Solid State Drive) — FLASH memory; FAST (500 MB/s SATA, 7000 MB/s PCIe NVMe); no moving parts; quiet; lower power; pricier per GB but gap closing. Samsung, Crucial, Kingston. NVMe standard. (3) Optical — CD (700 MB, 1982 — music discs, data CD-ROM), DVD (4.7-9 GB, 1996 — movies, software), BLU-RAY (25-100 GB, 2006 — HD-4K video). Declining with streaming. (4) CLOUD storage — Google Drive, OneDrive, iCloud, Dropbox. MEMORY HIERARCHY: (by speed decreasing, capacity increasing): CPU Registers → L1 cache → L2 cache → L3 cache → RAM → SSD → HDD → Cloud / Tape. Trade-off: SPEED vs SIZE vs COST. ACCESS times: Register <1 ns; L1 ~1 ns; L2 ~3 ns; L3 ~15 ns; RAM ~100 ns; SSD ~100 µs; HDD ~10 ms; network/cloud ~100 ms. Computer architects design memory hierarchy to hide latency + maximise throughput. loses data on power loss; stores data + running programs for CPU access; different from ROM (non-volatile).

cards.front:
An OPERATING SYSTEM (OS) is:

(A) Hardware of computer
(B) SYSTEM SOFTWARE that manages hardware + software resources + services to user + application programs
(C) Anti-virus
(D) A type of RAM
cards.back:
(B) SYSTEM SOFTWARE that manages hardware + software resources + services to user + application programs

Science, Tech & Defence — OPERATING SYSTEM (OS) — CORE SYSTEM SOFTWARE that: (1) MANAGES HARDWARE (CPU, RAM, disk, peripherals); (2) PROVIDES SERVICES to applications; (3) MANAGES FILES + processes + memory + network; (4) PROVIDES USER INTERFACE (CLI + GUI). WITHOUT OS, computer is unusable. FUNCTIONS: (1) PROCESS management (schedule tasks across CPU cores); (2) MEMORY management (virtual memory, paging); (3) FILE management (directories, permissions, access); (4) DEVICE management (drivers for peripherals); (5) SECURITY (access control, user accounts, firewall); (6) NETWORKING (protocols, sockets); (7) USER INTERFACE (shell, GUI — windowing, menus, buttons). DESKTOP OS: (1) MICROSOFT WINDOWS — dominant on PCs. Version history: Windows 3.1 (1992), 95, 98, ME, XP (2001, very popular), Vista, 7 (2009, beloved), 8, 10 (2015), 11 (2021), 12 upcoming. Market share ~70% of desktops. (2) macOS (Apple) — BSD Unix-based; Snow Leopard, Lion, Mountain Lion, Mavericks, Yosemite, Sierra, High Sierra, Mojave, Catalina, Big Sur (11), Monterey (12), Ventura (13), Sonoma (14), Sequoia (15). Since M1 ARM chips (2020) — transition to Apple Silicon. ~15% desktop share. (3) LINUX — OPEN-SOURCE UNIX-like; developed by Linus Torvalds (1991, Finland). Distributions: Ubuntu, Fedora, Debian, Arch, Red Hat Enterprise Linux, Mint, Manjaro. Kernel = LINUX; full OS = GNU/Linux. <5% desktop share but DOMINANT on SERVERS (~70%), supercomputers (100% of TOP500), embedded systems, Android base. (4) Chrome OS — Google; cloud-first laptops (Chromebooks); popular in education. MOBILE OS: (1) ANDROID — Google; Linux-based; open-source (AOSP); ~70% of global smartphones (2024). Versions: Cupcake, Donut, Eclair... Oreo, Pie, Android 10/11/12/13/14/15 (alphabetic dessert codenames dropped after 9). (2) iOS — Apple iPhone/iPad; BSD/Darwin-based. Versions iOS 1 (2007) through iOS 18 (2024). ~30% global share. (3) HarmonyOS (Huawei) — after US ban of Google; China-focused. (4) KaiOS — feature phones (Jio Phone in India based on KaiOS). (5) Obsolete: Windows Phone, BlackBerry, Symbian, Palm. EMBEDDED OS: (1) RTOS (Real-Time) — VxWorks, FreeRTOS, QNX. (2) Linux variants for routers/IoT. SERVER OS: Linux dominates cloud (AWS Linux, Ubuntu Server, Red Hat, CentOS); Windows Server for enterprise; UNIX legacy (Solaris, HP-UX, AIX) declining. INDIAN OS initiative: BHARAT OS (BharOS) by IIT Madras startup (2023) — stripped-down AOSP with no Google apps; NAVIC integration; for govt + security use. BOSS Linux (Bharat Operating System Solutions) by C-DAC — desktop + school + thin client editions. e.g., Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS.

cards.front:
The INTERNET is:

(A) Same as World Wide Web
(B) A GLOBAL NETWORK OF NETWORKS connecting billions of devices via TCP/IP protocols; WWW is just ONE service running on it
(C) Only accessible via Chrome
(D) A computer
cards.back:
(B) A GLOBAL NETWORK OF NETWORKS connecting billions of devices via TCP/IP protocols; WWW is just ONE service running on it

Science, Tech & Defence — INTERNET — global network of interconnected networks; billions of computers + IoT devices connected. ORIGINATED as ARPANET (1969, US Department of Defense research) — first message 'LO' sent 29 Oct 1969 from UCLA to SRI Stanford — trying to type 'LOGIN' but system crashed. 1983 — ARPANET switched to TCP/IP (by Vint Cerf + Bob Kahn) — 'Birthday of the Internet'. 1990 — ARPANET retired. Internet opened for commercial use 1991-93. INDIA: first internet connectivity = 15 Aug 1995 via VSNL. BSNL + MTNL + private ISPs followed. KEY PROTOCOLS: (1) TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol) — foundation. Connection-oriented reliable data transfer. (2) UDP — faster, no reliability guarantee (for streaming, DNS, gaming). (3) IP addresses — IPv4 (32-bit, 4.3 billion, running out; like 192.168.0.1) + IPv6 (128-bit, virtually unlimited; like 2001:0db8:85a3::8a2e). (4) DNS (Domain Name System) — translates domain names (google.com) to IP addresses. 13 root DNS servers worldwide (with anycast copies). (5) HTTP/HTTPS — web protocol. (6) SMTP (email send) + IMAP/POP3 (email receive). (7) FTP (file transfer). (8) SSH (secure shell). INTERNET vs WWW: (a) INTERNET = the INFRASTRUCTURE (physical + logical network). (b) WWW (World Wide Web) = an APPLICATION / service on Internet; hypertext documents accessed via HTTP using browsers. Invented by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN (1989-91). OTHER Internet services: email, FTP, VoIP, streaming, gaming, SSH, torrents, cloud computing, IoT. WEB BROWSERS: (1) GOOGLE CHROME — ~65% global share. (2) SAFARI (Apple) — ~18%. (3) MICROSOFT EDGE — ~5%. (4) FIREFOX (Mozilla) — ~3%. (5) Opera, Brave, DuckDuckGo, Tor Browser. SEARCH ENGINES: (1) GOOGLE (1998, Larry Page + Sergey Brin, Stanford PhD students; PageRank algorithm) — ~90% search share. (2) BING (Microsoft) — 3%, boosted by ChatGPT. (3) Yahoo, Baidu (China), Yandex (Russia), DuckDuckGo, Ecosia. SOCIAL MEDIA: Facebook/Meta (2004, Mark Zuckerberg, 3B users), YouTube (2005), Instagram (2010), WhatsApp (2009, Jan Koum + Brian Acton; FB bought 2014), X/Twitter (2006, Jack Dorsey; Musk bought 2022), TikTok (2016, Bytedance China; banned in India 2020), Snapchat, LinkedIn, Reddit, Pinterest, Telegram, Discord. INDIAN social media: Koo (now shut), Sharechat, Josh (short video), Chingari, Roposo. INTERNET GOVERNANCE: (1) ICANN (Internet Corp for Assigned Names + Numbers, 1998) — manages DNS + IP addresses. (2) IETF — Internet Engineering Task Force, technical standards (RFCs). (3) W3C — web standards. (4) IANA. INDIA INTERNET STATS: ~830 million users (2024); 2nd largest online population after China; Jio revolutionised with cheap data (2016 launch); 5G rollout 2022.

cards.front:
The GENERATIONS OF COMPUTERS are characterised by their underlying hardware technology. The THIRD generation used:

(A) Vacuum tubes
(B) INTEGRATED CIRCUITS (ICs)
(C) Microprocessors only
(D) Transistors only
cards.back:
(B) INTEGRATED CIRCUITS (ICs)

Science, Tech & Defence — GENERATIONS OF COMPUTERS — by dominant hardware technology: (1) 1ST GENERATION (1940-56) — VACUUM TUBES. Large (fill rooms), hot, fragile, power-hungry. ENIAC (1946, 18,000 tubes, 30 tons, 150 kW), UNIVAC I (1951). Programmed via wires + switches; machine code + assembly. Operated in days, often failing; HUGE heat dissipation. (2) 2ND GENERATION (1956-63) — TRANSISTORS. Invented 1947 at Bell Labs by Bardeen, Brattain, Shockley (Nobel Physics 1956). Solid-state; smaller + faster + cooler + more reliable than tubes. Enabled COMMERCIAL expansion. IBM 1401 (most-sold 2nd-gen, 10,000+ units), IBM 7094, CDC 1604. HIGH-LEVEL LANGUAGES emerged: FORTRAN (1957, IBM, John Backus — 'formula translation', scientific computing), COBOL (1959, US DoD, Grace Hopper — business data processing), ALGOL, LISP. (3) 3RD GENERATION (1964-71) — INTEGRATED CIRCUITS (ICs). Jack Kilby at Texas Instruments + Robert Noyce at Fairchild Semiconductor (1958-59) — Nobel Physics 2000 to Kilby. Multiple transistors on SINGLE SILICON CHIP. IBM System/360 (1964, revolutionary — compatible family). MINICOMPUTERS emerged (DEC PDP series). TIMESHARING OS (Multics → UNIX). Keyboards + monitors replaced punch cards. (4) 4TH GENERATION (1971-PRESENT) — MICROPROCESSORS (CPU on a single chip). INTEL 4004 (1971) — world's first microprocessor (4-bit, 2,300 transistors, Faggin + Hoff + Mazor). Intel 8008, 8080, 8086 (x86 birth), 80286, 386, 486, Pentium series. Apple II (1977), IBM PC (1981), Macintosh (1984). Rise of PC industry: Microsoft (1975 Gates + Allen), Apple (1976 Jobs + Wozniak + Wayne). Graphical User Interface (Xerox PARC → Apple → Microsoft). Internet explosion 1990s. SMARTPHONES 2007+ (iPhone). Today: 10+ billion transistors per chip; 3nm process. (5) 5TH GENERATION (future/present) — AI, QUANTUM COMPUTING, NEUROMORPHIC, PARALLEL PROCESSING. ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (LLMs like GPT-4, Claude, Gemini, Llama since 2017 transformer paper). QUANTUM computers (IBM Condor 1,121 qubits 2023; Google Sycamore 53 qubits 2019 supremacy claim; IBM Osprey, IBM System Two). NATURAL LANGUAGE UI becoming standard. AI-CHIPS (Nvidia H100/B200, Google TPU, AMD MI300, Apple M-series Neural Engine). COMPUTER SIZE evolution: ROOM-SIZED (1st gen) → desk-sized → desktop → laptop → smartphone → wearable → ubiquitous IoT. Moore's Law (doubling transistors every 2 years) drove this — slowing down since ~2016 but continuing via 3D stacking, chiplets, new materials (GaN, diamond). INDIA: PARAM 8000 (1991, C-DAC, Pune) — first Indian supercomputer; PARAM SIDDHI-AI (2020, ~5.2 PF) one of world's top 100. starting mid-1960s; microscopic transistors on silicon chip; enabled minicomputers + faster, cheaper, smaller.

cards.front:
The PROGRAMMING LANGUAGE created by GUIDO VAN ROSSUM in 1991 and now most popular for AI + data science is:

(A) Java
(B) PYTHON
(C) C++
(D) JavaScript
cards.back:
(B) PYTHON

Science, Tech & Defence — PYTHON — high-level, interpreted, dynamically-typed programming language. Created by GUIDO VAN ROSSUM (Dutch programmer) in 1989-91 at CWI Netherlands, released 1991. Named after 'Monty Python' comedy. Guido was called 'BDFL' (Benevolent Dictator For Life) for Python until stepping down 2018. DESIGN PHILOSOPHY: 'The Zen of Python' (by Tim Peters) — 'Beautiful is better than ugly; Explicit is better than implicit; Simple is better than complex; Readability counts; There should be one + preferably only one obvious way to do it.' VERSIONS: Python 2 (2000; deprecated end 2019) + Python 3 (2008, current — 3.13 latest 2024). Not backward-compatible across 2/3. STRENGTHS: (1) READABLE + CONCISE; (2) HUGE ECOSYSTEM — 500,000+ packages on PyPI; (3) GLUE LANGUAGE — bridges C/C++ + Java/other systems. LIBRARIES: (a) DATA SCIENCE: NumPy (arrays), pandas (dataframes), SciPy, Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly. (b) ML/AI: TensorFlow (Google), PyTorch (Meta), JAX (Google), scikit-learn, Keras, Hugging Face transformers, LangChain. (c) WEB: Django, Flask, FastAPI, Streamlit. (d) AUTOMATION: Selenium, BeautifulSoup, Requests. (e) GAME: Pygame. Python is the language of choice for AI RESEARCH + MACHINE LEARNING due to these libraries. POPULAR PROGRAMMING LANGUAGES (TIOBE index + IEEE Spectrum 2024): (1) PYTHON — #1; used in Google, Netflix, Instagram, Dropbox, NASA. (2) C — low-level system programming; OS kernels (Linux, Windows), embedded. (3) JAVA — enterprise, Android, banking; 'Write Once Run Anywhere' via JVM. (4) C++ — game engines, browsers, HPC, systems; OOP extension of C. (5) JAVASCRIPT / TypeScript — web browsers (front-end); Node.js (back-end). Ubiquitous. (6) C# (Microsoft) — enterprise, Windows, Unity gaming. (7) SQL — databases (declarative; Structured Query Language, 1970s IBM). (8) Go / Golang (Google 2009) — Cloud, concurrency. (9) RUST (Mozilla 2010) — memory-safe, systems. (10) SWIFT (Apple 2014) — iOS/Mac apps. (11) KOTLIN (JetBrains 2011) — Android preferred since 2017. (12) RUBY — Rails web framework. (13) R — statistics, data visualisation. (14) MATLAB — engineering, scientific. (15) SCALA, Elixir, Haskell, Clojure — functional. PARADIGMS: (1) PROCEDURAL (C, Pascal, BASIC); (2) OBJECT-ORIENTED (Java, C++, Python, C#); (3) FUNCTIONAL (Haskell, Lisp, Scheme, Erlang); (4) DECLARATIVE (SQL, Prolog, HTML); (5) SCRIPTING (Python, Perl, Ruby, JavaScript). FIRST PROGRAMMING LANGUAGE: FORTRAN (1957, IBM). LISP (1958, McCarthy) oldest used today. COBOL still runs 70% of banking + govt (legacy). AGE OF AI: 'Prompt engineering' emerging as programming paradigm with LLMs; code assistants (GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude) transforming coding productivity.

VERSIONS: Python 2 (2000; deprecated end 2019) + Python 3 (2008, current — 3.13 latest 2024). Not backward-compatible across 2/3. STRENGTHS: (1) READABLE + CONCISE; (2) HUGE ECOSYSTEM — 500,000+ packages on PyPI; (3) GLUE LANGUAGE — bridges C/C++ + Java/other systems. LIBRARIES: (a) DATA SCIENCE: NumPy (arrays), pandas (dataframes), SciPy, Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly. (b) ML/AI: TensorFlow (Google), PyTorch (Meta), JAX (Google), scikit-learn, Keras, Hugging Face transformers, LangChain. (c) WEB: Django, Flask, FastAPI, Streamlit. (d) AUTOMATION: Selenium, BeautifulSoup, Requests. (e) GAME: Pygame. Python is the language of choice for AI RESEARCH + MACHINE LEARNING due to these libraries. POPULAR PROGRAMMING LANGUAGES (TIOBE index + IEEE Spectrum 2024): (1) PYTHON — #1; used in Google, Netflix, Instagram, Dropbox, NASA. (2) C — low-level system programming; OS kernels (Linux, Windows), embedded. (3) JAVA — enterprise, Android, banking; 'Write Once Run Anywhere' via JVM. (4) C++ — game engines, browsers, HPC, systems; OOP extension of C. (5) JAVASCRIPT / TypeScript — web browsers (front-end); Node.js (back-end). Ubiquitous. (6) C# (Microsoft) — enterprise, Windows, Unity gaming. (7) SQL — databases (declarative; Structured Query Language, 1970s IBM). (8) Go / Golang (Google 2009) — Cloud, concurrency. (9) RUST (Mozilla 2010) — memory-safe, systems. (10) SWIFT (Apple 2014) — iOS/Mac apps. (11) KOTLIN (JetBrains 2011) — Android preferred since 2017. (12) RUBY — Rails web framework. (13) R — statistics, data visualisation. (14) MATLAB — engineering, scientific. (15) SCALA, Elixir, Haskell, Clojure — functional. PARADIGMS: (1) PROCEDURAL (C, Pascal, BASIC); (2) OBJECT-ORIENTED (Java, C++, Python, C#); (3) FUNCTIONAL (Haskell, Lisp, Scheme, Erlang); (4) DECLARATIVE (SQL, Prolog, HTML); (5) SCRIPTING (Python, Perl, Ruby, JavaScript). FIRST PROGRAMMING LANGUAGE: FORTRAN (1957, IBM). LISP (1958, McCarthy) oldest used today. COBOL still runs 70% of banking + govt (legacy). AGE OF AI: 'Prompt engineering' emerging as programming paradigm with LLMs; code assistants (GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude) transforming coding productivity.

cards.front:
A COMPUTER VIRUS is:

(A) A hardware failure
(B) MALICIOUS SOFTWARE that replicates by modifying other programs; types include worms, trojans, ransomware, spyware, adware
(C) A browser extension
(D) A type of RAM
cards.back:
(B) MALICIOUS SOFTWARE that replicates by modifying other programs; types include worms, trojans, ransomware, spyware, adware

Science, Tech & Defence — COMPUTER VIRUS — malicious software that self-replicates by attaching itself to other programs. Broader category: MALWARE (MALicious softWARE). FIRST virus in wild: Creeper (1971, on ARPANET, not truly malicious). First PC virus: Brain (1986, Pakistani — Amjad + Basit Farooq Alvi, to protect their own software from piracy; went global accidentally). TYPES of MALWARE: (1) VIRUS — attaches to executables/files; spreads when user runs. (2) WORM — self-replicates across networks without human action; Morris Worm (1988 first big; ILOVEYOU 2000, Conficker 2008, WannaCry 2017, Stuxnet 2010). (3) TROJAN HORSE — disguised as legitimate software; doesn't self-replicate but delivers payload. Trickbot, Zeus. (4) RANSOMWARE — encrypts files, demands ransom in crypto. WannaCry (2017) hit 200,000 systems in 150 countries incl NHS UK, Indian banks; Petya/NotPetya (2017), Ryuk, REvil, LockBit. Pay 0.1-10 BTC. (5) SPYWARE — secretly monitors user; logs keystrokes, exfiltrates data. Pegasus (NSO Group, Israel — sold to governments; used to target journalists + dissidents; controversy 2021 Forbidden Stories + Amnesty exposure). (6) ADWARE — bombards ads; bundled in freeware. (7) ROOTKITS — hide deep in OS; hardest to remove. (8) BOTNETS — network of compromised 'zombie' computers controlled by attacker; used for DDoS, spam, crypto mining. Mirai (2016 IoT botnet). (9) KEYLOGGERS; (10) CRYPTOMINERS; (11) BACKDOORS; (12) SCAREWARE. PROTECTION: (1) ANTIVIRUS — Norton, McAfee, Kaspersky (Russian — banned in several countries since 2022), Bitdefender, Windows Defender (built-in free), Avast, ESET, Quick Heal (Indian). (2) FIREWALL — OS-built (Windows Defender Firewall) + network. (3) SOFTWARE UPDATES — patch security holes. (4) STRONG PASSWORDS + PASSWORD MANAGERS (LastPass, 1Password, Bitwarden). (5) 2FA / MFA (Two-Factor Authentication) — SMS/app-based OTP/security key. (6) BACKUPS — air-gapped or immutable cloud. (7) SAFE BROWSING — avoid suspicious links, verify URLs. (8) PHISHING awareness. (9) VPN for public Wi-Fi. (10) Don't use cracked software. MAJOR CYBER INCIDENTS: (1) Stuxnet (2010) — US-Israeli joint; destroyed Iranian nuclear centrifuges. (2) Sony Pictures hack (2014) — N. Korea, The Interview movie. (3) Equifax breach (2017) — 147M records. (4) AIIMS Delhi ransomware (Nov 2022) — ₹200 cr demand; 5 servers encrypted. (5) 2021 — Air India + Domino's India breaches. INDIA cyber governance: CERT-In (Indian Computer Emergency Response Team, under MeitY, est 2004) — monitors + responds; CYBER CRIME helpline 1930; NCIIPC (Critical Infrastructure); DIGITAL PERSONAL DATA PROTECTION (DPDP) ACT 2023 — privacy law; IT ACT 2000 — primary cyber law + amended. RBI Cyber Security Framework for banks. India 3rd largest cybercrime victim after US + China.

cards.front:
ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) term was coined in 1956 by:

(A) Alan Turing
(B) JOHN McCARTHY
(C) Marvin Minsky
(D) Claude Shannon
cards.back:
(B) JOHN McCARTHY

Science, Tech & Defence — ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) — 'intelligence' exhibited by machines. TERM coined by JOHN MCCARTHY (Stanford + Dartmouth + MIT professor) for the 1956 DARTMOUTH SUMMER RESEARCH PROJECT ON AI — 6-8 week workshop at Dartmouth College (Hanover, New Hampshire); considered the FOUNDING event of AI as a field. ATTENDEES included: John McCarthy, Marvin Minsky (MIT), Claude Shannon (Bell Labs, information theory), Nathaniel Rochester (IBM), Allen Newell + Herbert Simon (CMU — later Nobel Econ + Turing). EARLIER: Alan Turing (1950) — 'Computing Machinery + Intelligence' paper + TURING TEST ('Can machines think?'). AI MILESTONES: (1) 1956 Dartmouth. (2) 1957 Perceptron (Rosenblatt) — first neural network. (3) 1966 ELIZA (Weizenbaum) — early chatbot. (4) 1970s-80s AI 'WINTERS' (funding + interest dried due to overpromising + under-delivery). (5) 1997 — IBM DEEP BLUE defeated world chess champion GARRY KASPAROV 3.5-2.5. (6) 2004 — DARPA Grand Challenge self-driving (no one finished initially). (7) 2011 — IBM WATSON won Jeopardy! vs Ken Jennings + Brad Rutter. (8) 2012 — DEEP LEARNING revolution; Krizhevsky-Sutskever-Hinton's AlexNet won ImageNet competition using GPUs + convolutional neural networks. (9) 2016 — GOOGLE DEEPMIND's ALPHAGO defeated world Go champion LEE SEDOL 4-1 (earlier Fan Hui). Go was considered untouchable by AI for decades. (10) 2017 — TRANSFORMER architecture paper 'Attention is All You Need' (Vaswani et al., Google). Foundation of LLMs. (11) 2018 — BERT (Google), GPT (OpenAI); rise of pretrained language models. (12) 2020 — AlphaFold2 (DeepMind) — 50-year-old protein-folding problem solved; Nobel Chemistry 2024 shared. (13) Nov 2022 — CHATGPT (OpenAI, GPT-3.5) released; mass adoption of generative AI. (14) 2023+ — explosion: GPT-4 (OpenAI), Claude (Anthropic — Dario + Daniela Amodei), Gemini (Google), Llama (Meta, open-source), Mistral (France), Grok (xAI). Stable Diffusion, Midjourney, DALL-E for images; Sora + Runway for video; Whisper for speech. TYPES OF AI: (1) ANI (Artificial Narrow Intelligence) — domain-specific (chess AI, image recognition, voice assistants); we are here. (2) AGI (Artificial General Intelligence) — human-level across domains; goal of OpenAI, DeepMind, Anthropic; not yet achieved. (3) ASI (Artificial Super Intelligence) — beyond human; hypothetical; existential concerns. SUBFIELDS: machine learning (ML), deep learning (neural networks), natural language processing (NLP), computer vision, robotics, reinforcement learning, generative AI, agent-based systems. INDIA: AI policy 'AI for ALL' by NITI Aayog; INDIAai portal; Bhashini (NLP for Indian languages); Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) + AI intersection; GoI's IndiaAI Mission ₹10,372 cr approved 2024. at the DARTMOUTH SUMMER RESEARCH PROJECT ON AI, widely regarded as the FOUNDING event of AI as a field.

cards.front:
The BRAIN of a computer is the:

(A) ROM
(B) CPU
(C) Hard disk
(D) Monitor
cards.back:
(B) CPU

Science, Tech & Defence — CPU = Central Processing Unit — executes instructions, does arithmetic & logic. Comprises ALU + CU + registers. ROM = Read-Only Memory (firmware). Hard disk / SSD = persistent storage. Monitor = output device.
cards.storedExplanation: CPU = Central Processing Unit — executes instructions, does arithmetic & logic. Comprises ALU + CU + registers. ROM = Read-Only Memory (firmware). Hard disk / SSD = persistent storage. Monitor = output device.

cards.front:
RAM stands for:

(A) Read-Only Access Memory
(B) Random Access Memory
(C) Rapid Action Memory
(D) Remote Access Memory
cards.back:
(B) Random Access Memory

Science, Tech & Defence — RAM — Random Access Memory. Volatile (lost on power-off), fast, stores data currently being processed. ROM — Read-Only Memory, non-volatile, stores firmware / BIOS. Typical laptops: 8-32 GB RAM, 256 GB - 2 TB SSD.

cards.front:
Match the FULL FORM with its ACRONYM. A. HTTP.  B. URL.  C. LAN.  D. SMTP. List-II: 1. Hypertext Transfer Protocol.  2. Uniform Resource Locator.  3. Local Area Network.  4. Simple Mail Transfer Protocol.

(A) A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4
(B) A-2, B-1, C-3, D-4
(C) A-1, B-3, C-2, D-4
(D) A-1, B-2, C-4, D-3
cards.back:
(A) A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4

Science, Tech & Defence — HTTP — app-layer protocol for web. URL — address of a web resource. LAN — network within a limited area (vs WAN, MAN). SMTP — protocol for sending email. Bonus: POP3/IMAP — receiving email. FTP — File Transfer Protocol.

cards.front:
One KILOBYTE (KB) equals:

(A) 1,000 bits
(B) 1,024 bytes (binary) or 1,000 bytes (decimal)
(C) 1,024 gigabytes
(D) 1 byte
cards.back:
(B) 1,024 bytes (binary) or 1,000 bytes (decimal)

Science, Tech & Defence — Classical/binary: 1 KB = 2¹⁰ = 1,024 bytes. Decimal/SI: 1 kB = 1,000 bytes; 1 KiB = 1,024 bytes (IEC standard). In everyday use, 'KB' usually means 1,024 bytes. Hierarchy: B → KB → MB → GB → TB → PB.

cards.front:
The FATHER OF COMPUTER is considered to be:

(A) Alan Turing
(B) Charles Babbage
(C) Tim Berners-Lee
(D) John von Neumann
cards.back:
(B) Charles Babbage

Science, Tech & Defence — Charles Babbage — designed the Analytical Engine (1837), a general-purpose mechanical computer. Ada Lovelace wrote the first 'programs' for it. Turing formalised computability (Turing machine). Von Neumann designed the stored-program architecture. Berners-Lee invented the WWW.

Which of the following is an OPERATING SYSTEM?

(A) Microsoft Word
(B) Linux
(C) Python
(D) Google Chrome
cards.back:
(B) Linux

Science, Tech & Defence — Linux — open-source OS (kernel by Linus Torvalds, 1991). Other OSes: Windows, macOS, Android, iOS. Word = application. Python = programming language. Chrome = web browser.

cards.front:
'Firewall' in a computer system primarily:

(A) Prevents hardware overheating
(B) Monitors and controls incoming/outgoing network traffic based on security rules
(C) Acts as an antivirus
(D) Increases internet speed
cards.back:
(B) Monitors and controls incoming/outgoing network traffic based on security rules

Science, Tech & Defence — Firewall — network-security device (hardware, software, or combination). Filters traffic to block unauthorised access. Works with antivirus + intrusion detection. Different from antivirus (file scanning) — can be deployed at router or OS level.

cards.front:
The INTEGRATED GUIDED MISSILE DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME (IGMDP), started in 1983, was led by:

(A) Homi Bhabha
(B) Dr A.P.J. ABDUL KALAM
(C) Satish Dhawan
(D) Vikram Sarabhai
cards.back:
(B) Dr A.P.J. ABDUL KALAM

Science, Tech & Defence — IGMDP (Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme) — Indian ministry of defence's ambitious programme (1983-2008) to develop indigenous missiles. LAUNCHED 26 JULY 1983. Director: Dr A.P.J. ABDUL KALAM (later 11th President of India, 2002-07; 'MISSILE MAN OF INDIA'). AIMED to end India's dependence on foreign arms; fund allocated ₹389 crore initially. 5 MISSILE PROJECTS: (1) PRITHVI — surface-to-surface TACTICAL ballistic; range 150-350 km; Army (Prithvi-I 150 km), Air Force (Prithvi-II 250 km), Navy (Prithvi-III / Dhanush 350 km). First tested 25 Feb 1988. (2) AGNI — long-range ballistic missile series (originally, a tech demonstrator; later separate IRBM programme). (3) TRISHUL — short-range surface-to-air; 9 km (tested but not productised). (4) AKASH — medium-range surface-to-air; 30 km; INDUCTED by Army + IAF; similar to US Patriot. (5) NAG — anti-tank guided missile; range 4-8 km; 'fire + forget'; mounted on Nag Missile Carrier (NAMICA). PRINCIPAL DEVELOPER: DRDO (DEFENCE RESEARCH + DEVELOPMENT ORGANISATION) — India's premier military R&D body (est. 1958). DRDO has 50+ laboratories: DRDL (Hyderabad, missiles), BrahMos (JV with Russia), CRL Chandigarh, CVRDE Avadi (combat vehicles), LRDE (radars), RCI Hyderabad, ITR Chandipur (Interim Test Range — missile firing off Odisha coast). CURRENT DRDO CHAIRMAN: Dr. Samir V. Kamat (2023-). IGMDP officially CONCLUDED 8 Jan 2008 — succeeded by standalone missile programmes: AGNI (strategic ballistic, upgraded), BRAHMOS (supersonic cruise, Indo-Russian JV 2001; 290 km initially, 450-800 km now), NIRBHAY (subsonic cruise, 1,500 km), ASTRA (BVRAAM, air-to-air), QRSAM (Quick Reaction SAM), Helina (Helicopter-launched NAG). DR. KALAM's ROLE: served as DRDO chief, Scientific Adviser to Raksha Mantri, Secretary DRDO; led missile programme 1983-99; later headed POKHRAN-II nuclear tests (May 1998) as Principal Scientific Advisor. 11th PRESIDENT 2002-07; Bharat Ratna 1997; died 27 Jul 2015 in Shillong while giving lecture — aged 83. 'Missile Man of India'; developed PRITHVI, AGNI, AKASH, TRISHUL, NAG.

cards.front:
India's LONGEST-range strategic ballistic missile, capable of hitting targets beyond 5000 km, is:

(A) Agni-I
(B) AGNI-V (ICBM-class, range 5,000-8,000+ km; MIRV-capable from 2024 Mission Divyastra); first launched 2012
(C) Prithvi-III
(D) BrahMos
cards.back:
(B) AGNI-V (ICBM-class, range 5,000-8,000+ km; MIRV-capable from 2024 Mission Divyastra); first launched 2012

Science, Tech & Defence — AGNI SERIES — India's indigenous medium to intercontinental-range ballistic missiles; strategic nuclear deterrent. (1) AGNI-I — SRBM, single-stage, range 700-1,200 km; inducted 2004. (2) AGNI-II — MRBM, 2-stage, range 2,000-3,000 km; inducted 2011. (3) AGNI-III — IRBM, 2-stage, range 3,000-5,500 km; inducted 2011. (4) AGNI-IV — IRBM, 2-stage, range 3,500-4,000 km; 1 tonne warhead. Inducted 2014. (5) AGNI-V — ICBM-class, 3-stage, range 5,000-8,000+ km (officially 5,000+; unofficial estimates up to 8,000 km); strategically can hit ALL of China + much of Europe. First tested 19 April 2012 from Wheeler Island (Abdul Kalam Island). Inducted into Strategic Forces Command (SFC) 2023. MIRV VARIANT — 'MISSION DIVYASTRA' — first test on 11 MARCH 2024 — successful test of MIRV (Multiple Independently-targetable Re-entry Vehicle) capability on Agni-V. India became 6th MIRV-capable nation (USA, Russia, China, UK, France + India). (6) AGNI-VI / K-5 / K-6 — in development; rumoured 8,000-12,000 km ICBM; SLBM variants. SUBMARINE-LAUNCHED BALLISTIC MISSILES (SLBM) — K series (named for Abdul Kalam): (a) K-15 / B-05 SAGARIKA — 750 km, deployed on INS Arihant nuclear submarine since 2018. (b) K-4 — 3,500 km, tested successfully, being deployed on Arihant-class SSBNs. (c) K-5, K-6 — future, 5,000-6,000 km. INS ARIHANT (commissioned 2016) = India's first ballistic missile submarine. INS Arighaat (2024), Aridhaman (future) — S4/S4* follow-on SSBNs. STRATEGIC TRIAD (land, air, sea-based nuclear delivery) — India achieved with Arihant-class + Agni-V. cards.front:
BRAHMOS, the world's FASTEST cruise missile, is a joint venture between INDIA + which country?

(A) France
(B) RUSSIA (NPO Mashinostroyenia)
(C) Israel
(D) USA
cards.back:
(B) RUSSIA (NPO Mashinostroyenia)

Science, Tech & Defence — BRAHMOS — supersonic CRUISE MISSILE; JOINT VENTURE between India's DRDO + Russia's NPO Mashinostroyenia (NPOM). NAME: portmanteau of BRAHMAputra (India) + MOSkva (Russia). ESTABLISHED 1998 (JV signed by Dr. Kalam + Nikolai Mikhailov); company incorporated 2001. HEADQUARTERS: New Delhi (BrahMos Aerospace). FIRST TEST: 12 June 2001 from Chandipur (Odisha). SPECS: (1) SPEED — Mach 2.8 to 3.5 (nearly 3X speed of sound); world's FASTEST operational cruise missile. (2) RANGE — INITIAL 290 km (MTCR limit); EXTENDED to 450 km in 2017 after India joined MTCR (Missile Technology Control Regime) in 2016; 'BrahMos-ER' 500-800 km variant under development. (3) WARHEAD — 200-300 kg conventional (can carry nuclear but not a nuclear weapon system). (4) TWO-STAGE — solid booster + liquid-fuelled ramjet. (5) LENGTH 8.4m, diameter 0.6m. (6) LAUNCH PLATFORMS — LAND (Mobile Autonomous Launcher, 5-tube MAL), SHIP-launched (destroyers, frigates — INS Rajput first 2005; all new ships), SUBMARINE-launched (tested from INS Karanj), AIR-launched (integrated on Su-30MKI since 2016 — 'BrahMos-A' 2.5 tonne air variant; first live fire 2017). INDIA = FIRST country to have supersonic AIR-LAUNCHED CRUISE MISSILE. INDUCTED IN: (a) Indian Army (3 regiments + 4th under induction); (b) Indian Navy (30+ ships); (c) Indian Air Force (Su-30MKI squadron in Thanjavur). EXPORT: PHILIPPINES first export customer — signed Jan 2022, $375M deal for 3 batteries; delivery completed 2024. Other interested: Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, UAE. Also BrahMos-NG (Next Generation, smaller 1.5-tonne version, for Tejas LCA + MiG-29K + Rafale etc.) in development. BRAHMOS-II — HYPERSONIC (Mach 7-8), under development; JV with Russia. FAMOUSLY in March 2022, a BrahMos misfired from India (due to technical error, no warhead) and landed ~120km inside PAKISTAN (Mian Channu). Both countries handled it professionally; 3 IAF officers terminated. NO escalation. RAMJETS + SCRAMJETS: DRDO tested HSTDV (Hypersonic Technology Demonstrator Vehicle) in 2020 + 2022 — indigenous scramjet at Mach 6+; foundation for BrahMos-II + Shaurya hypersonic programmes. named after BRAHMAPUTRA + MOSKVA rivers; Mach 2.8-3.5; est. 1998, 1st test 2001.

cards.front:
The CHIEF OF DEFENCE STAFF (CDS), created in 2019 as India's top uniformed officer, was FIRST held by:

(A) General Bipin Rawat
(B) General Anil Chauhan
(C) Admiral Karambir Singh
(D) Air Chief Marshal Rakesh Bhadauria
cards.back:
(A) General Bipin Rawat

Science, Tech & Defence — CHIEF OF DEFENCE STAFF (CDS) — newly-created POST (Dec 2019) of SENIOR-MOST uniformed officer of Indian Armed Forces. Recommended by KARGIL REVIEW COMMITTEE (K. Subrahmanyam) 1999, Naresh Chandra Task Force 2012; finally announced by PM Modi on 15 Aug 2019 Independence Day speech. CREATED via: (1) Amendments to Services Acts; (2) New 'Department of Military Affairs' (DMA) in Ministry of Defence — headed by CDS (ex-officio Secretary, DMA). ROLE: (1) SINGLE-POINT MILITARY advisor to Defence Minister (previously 3 service chiefs gave separate advice). (2) Promote 'JOINTNESS' — tri-services integration. (3) Permanent Chairman of CHIEFS OF STAFF COMMITTEE (COSC). (4) Not operational commander — each service chief retains operational command. (5) Oversees theaterisation — reorganising forces into integrated theatre commands. (6) Nuclear Command Authority advisor. CDS 1: GENERAL BIPIN RAWAT (27th COAS); assumed office 1 Jan 2020. Previously Chief of Army Staff (2017-19). TRAGICALLY DIED in MI-17V5 helicopter CRASH on 8 DECEMBER 2021 near Coonoor, Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu — he, wife Madhulika Rawat + 11 others perished; only 1 survivor (Gp Capt Varun Singh, who later died of burns Dec 15). Shock across nation. Enquiry by Tri-Services: pilot error in low-visibility (cloud + mountain); helicopter impacted hillside. VACANT CDS post from 8 Dec 2021 – 30 Sep 2022. CDS 2: GENERAL ANIL CHAUHAN (assumed 30 Sep 2022). Former GOC-in-C of Eastern Command; Kargil war veteran. Also: Air Chief Marshal + Navy Chief eligible; first two CDS have been Army. Term: 3 years; age 65 max. STRATEGIC DIRECTION: India is working towards THEATRE COMMANDS — integrating Army, Navy, AF in geographic commands (instead of service-wise). Proposed: Western Theatre (vs Pakistan), Northern Theatre (vs China), Maritime Theatre. Currently 17 single-service commands (7 Army + 7 Air + 3 Navy); ANDAMAN + NICOBAR COMMAND (ANC) = India's ONLY existing joint service theatre command since 2001; STRATEGIC FORCES COMMAND (SFC) — nuclear. CDS + DMA drive this reorganisation. Global examples: USA's 11 combatant commands, China's 5 theatre commands. 1 Jan 2020 – 8 Dec 2021; killed in Coonoor helicopter crash.

cards.front:
India conducted its FIRST nuclear test, 'Smiling Buddha' (Pokhran-I), on:

(A) 11 May 1998
(B) 18 MAY 1974
(C) 26 January 1950
(D) 15 August 1976
cards.back:
(B) 18 MAY 1974

Science, Tech & Defence — INDIA's NUCLEAR TESTS — milestones: (1) POKHRAN-I / SMILING BUDDHA — 18 MAY 1974 (Buddha Purnima day, code named 'Smiling Buddha'). PM INDIRA GANDHI. Test at Pokhran, Jaisalmer, Rajasthan. Described as 'PEACEFUL NUCLEAR EXPLOSION' (PNE) to sidestep international obligations, though fuel was reactor-grade Plutonium. Yield ~8 kt (claimed; estimates 4-13 kt). Explosion went off in a 100m-deep shaft. Project led by BARC (Bhabha Atomic Research Centre) under Dr. RAJA RAMANNA (Project Director), with Dr. Homi Sethna (AEC Chairman), BASANTI DULAL NAG CHAUDHURI (ex-Scientific Adviser). INDIA's first PLUTONIUM used from CIRUS reactor (a Canadian-supplied heavy-water research reactor, contaminated with US heavy water). USA's + CANADA's reaction: sharp sanctions; end of civil nuclear cooperation; CANADA pulled out of NAPP; USA put India under strict tech sanctions. (2) POKHRAN-II / OPERATION SHAKTI — 11 + 13 MAY 1998. PM Atal Bihari VAJPAYEE; Principal Scientific Adviser Dr A.P.J. ABDUL KALAM coordinated; BARC director R. Chidambaram + DRDO + Atomic Energy Commission. 5 tests — 3 on 11 May 1998 + 2 on 13 May 1998. YIELDS: (a) 43 kt thermonuclear (hydrogen bomb) — disputed; some seismologists estimated 12-25 kt; Indian officials maintained 43 kt. (b) 12 kt fission. (c) 0.3 kt subkiloton. (d) 0.5 kt + 0.2 kt sub-kilotons on 13 May. Declared India as a NUCLEAR WEAPON STATE. SANCTIONS: UN + USA + G-7 imposed wide sanctions (mostly lifted by 2001). PAKISTAN's response: Chagai-I on 28 May 1998 (5 tests) + Chagai-II on 30 May (1 test) — bringing S. Asia into OVERT nuclear standoff. POST-1998: Subsequent elimination of sanctions with INDO-US CIVIL NUCLEAR DEAL 2005 (123 Agreement, Hyde Act); NSG waiver 2008; IAEA safeguards for civil reactors (2009). India now imports uranium (Kazakhstan, Russia, Canada) + civil nuclear cooperation with 14+ countries. 11 MAY = NATIONAL TECHNOLOGY DAY (declared 1999 by PM Vajpayee, commemorating Pokhran-II + AGNI + Hansa-3 aircraft tests). INDIA NEVER signed NPT (1968) or CTBT (1996). Follows 'NO FIRST USE' (NFU) nuclear doctrine + 'credible minimum deterrent'. STRATEGIC FORCES COMMAND (SFC, 2003) operates nuclear forces; POLITICAL COUNCIL of NCA (PM-led) has sole launch authority. Arsenal estimated ~170 warheads (SIPRI 2024). Pokhran, Rajasthan; declared 'peaceful nuclear explosion'; PM Indira Gandhi; yield ~8 kt.

cards.front:
INS VIKRANT, India's FIRST INDIGENOUS aircraft carrier, was commissioned on:

(A) 15 August 2022
(B) 2 SEPTEMBER 2022
(C) 26 January 2023
(D) 14 February 2022
cards.back:
(B) 2 SEPTEMBER 2022

Science, Tech & Defence — INS VIKRANT (R11) — INDIA's FIRST INDIGENOUSLY BUILT AIRCRAFT CARRIER. Commissioned 2 SEPTEMBER 2022 by PM Narendra Modi at COCHIN SHIPYARD LIMITED (CSL), Kerala. BUILT by CSL (PSU). COST: ~₹20,000 CRORE. TIMELINE: keel laid 2009; launched 2013; undocked 2015; sea trials 2021; delivered July 2022; commissioned Sep 2022. SPECIFICATIONS: Displacement 45,000 tonnes; length 262m; beam 62m; draught 8.4m; speed 28 knots (52 km/h); range 7,500 nautical miles; crew 1,600 (including 160 officers). AIR WING: 30 aircraft — MiG-29K fighters (operational), Kamov Ka-31 AEW helicopters, MH-60R Romeo anti-submarine helicopters, HAL Dhruv/ALH, HAL Rudra. TEJAS MK-1A LCA + LCA-Navy being developed. Twin Island design. PROPULSION: 4 GE LM2500 gas turbines (88 MW total); 75% indigenous content (Navy target). SIGNIFICANCE: (1) INDIA became 6th country to design + build its own aircraft carrier (after US, UK, Russia, France, China). (2) Revives NAME 'VIKRANT' from India's first aircraft carrier (HMS Hercules → INS Vikrant, commissioned 1961, retired 1997) — which operated in 1971 Bangladesh War (sinking PNS Ghazi attempt to ambush it). HISTORIC INS VIKRANT now a MUSEUM SHIP — though plans scrapped; ship scrapped in 2014 (controversial; partial parts converted into memorials). ROYAL ENFIELD launched 'Classic 350 Vikrant' in 2023 using metal from original Vikrant. CURRENT INDIAN NAVY FLEET (2024-25): (1) 2 AIRCRAFT CARRIERS: INS Vikramaditya (ex-Soviet/Russian Admiral Gorshkov, commissioned 2013, 44,500t) + INS Vikrant (2022, 45,000t). (2) NUCLEAR SUBMARINES: INS Arihant (SSBN, 6,000t, commissioned 2016, K-15/K-4 SLBMs); INS Arighaat (2024); INS Chakra-III (SSN leased from Russia 2025, successor to Chakra-II returned 2021). (3) CONVENTIONAL SUBMARINES: 17 (Kalvari/Scorpene class 5, Shishumar/Type-209 4, Sindhughosh/Kilo 7). (4) DESTROYERS: 11 (Kolkata-class 3, Delhi-class 3, Visakhapatnam-class 4, Rajput-class 1). (5) FRIGATES: 15. (6) Total ~155 ships + 240 aircraft. IAC-II / INS VISHAL (proposed 3rd carrier, 65,000t, CATOBAR with EMALS catapults) under debate. at Kochi; 45,000 tonnes; built by Cochin Shipyard Ltd; carries 30 aircraft (Mig-29K, Tejas, helos).
